title.zh: 卷419 列傳二百六 刘长佑 刘岳昭 岑毓英弟 毓宝
title.en: Volume 419 Biographies 206: Liu Zhangyou, Liu Yuezhao, Cen Yuyingdi, Yu Bao
title.raw: 卷419 列傳二百六 刘长佑 刘岳昭 岑毓英弟 毓宝

sentences.zh: 列傳二百六

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Two Hundred Six.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 206.

sentences.zh: 劉長佑劉岳昭岑毓英弟毓寶

translations.literal: Liu Zhangyou, Liu Yuezhao, Cen Yuying, and Cen Yuying's younger brother Yu Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhangyou, Liu Yuezhao, Cen Yuying, and Yu Bao.

sentences.zh: 劉長佑，字印渠，湖南新寧人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhangyou, courtesy name Yin Qu, was a native of Xinning in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhangyou, styled Yin Qu, was a native of Xinning in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十九年拔貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of the Daoguang reign, he was selected as a tribute graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of the Daoguang reign, he was selected as a tribute graduate from the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 與同縣江忠源友。

translations.literal: He was friends with Jiang Zhongyuan of the same county.
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with Jiang Zhongyuan, a fellow townsman.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，忠源率鄉勇赴廣西助剿，長佑從。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Xianfeng reign, Zhongyuan led local militia to Guangxi to assist in suppression campaigns, and Zhangyou followed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xianfeng reign, Jiang Zhongyuan led local militia to Guangxi to help suppress the rebels, and Liu Zhangyou went with him.

sentences.zh: 粵匪自桂林走湖南，忠源破之於蓑衣渡，長佑有贊畫功，獎敘教諭。

translations.literal: The Cantonese rebels fled from Guilin into Hunan; Zhongyuan defeated them at Suoyi Crossing; Zhangyou had merit in planning; he was rewarded with appointment as an Instructor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Cantonese rebels retreated from Guilin into Hunan, Jiang Zhongyuan routed them at Suoyi Crossing; Liu Zhangyou was credited with strategic planning and was rewarded with appointment as an Instructor.

sentences.zh: 又從破瀏陽徵義堂會匪，擢知縣。

translations.literal: He again followed in the defeat of the Zhengyitang bandit association in Liuyang, and was promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He again took part in the defeat of the Zhengyitang bandits in Liuyang and was promoted to county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 三年，平衡山土匪，擢同知直隸州。

translations.literal: In the third year, he pacified the bandits at Pingshan and was promoted to Sub-Prefect of Zhili Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Xianfeng reign, he pacified the bandits at Pingshan and was promoted to Sub-Prefect of Zhili Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 忠源援湖北，遇賊崇、通間，長佑自長沙馳援，戰於通城，大破之，自是獨領一軍。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan went to aid Hubei and encountered bandits between Chongyang and Tongcheng; Zhangyou rushed from Changsha to reinforce him, fought at Tongcheng, and inflicted a great defeat; from then on he independently commanded an army.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Zhongyuan went to relieve Hubei and clashed with the rebels between Chongyang and Tongcheng, Liu Zhangyou raced from Changsha to his aid, fought at Tongcheng, and won a crushing victory; from that point he commanded an army of his own.

sentences.zh: 忠源守南昌，長佑偕羅澤南赴援，解吉安圍，分兵克泰和，擢知府。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan defended Nanchang; Zhangyou went with Luo Zena to reinforce him, lifted the siege of Ji'an, sent detachments to capture Taihe, and was promoted to Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: While Jiang Zhongyuan held Nanchang, Liu Zhangyou marched with Luo Zena to relieve him, broke the siege of Ji'an, detached troops to capture Taihe, and was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 忠源殉廬州，長佑偕忠源弟忠濬率千人馳援弗及，大憤，誓滅賊。

translations.literal: When Zhongyuan died at Luzhou, Zhangyou went with Zhongyuan's younger brother Zhongjun at the head of a thousand men to rush to his aid but arrived too late; greatly enraged, he swore to exterminate the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiang Zhongyuan fell at Luzhou, Liu Zhangyou and Jiang Zhongyuan's younger brother Zhongjun led a thousand men in a desperate rush to save him but arrived too late; burning with rage, he swore to destroy the rebels utterly.

sentences.zh: 五年，江忠淑剿東安賊不利，駱秉章以長佑兼統其眾，所部始盛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Jiang Zhongshu met with ill success in suppressing the bandits at Dong'an; Luo Bingzhang had Zhangyou also take command of his forces, and his command then began to flourish.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Jiang Zhongshu's campaign against the bandits at Dong'an went badly; Luo Bingzhang put Liu Zhangyou in joint command of his troops as well, and from then on his forces grew strong.

sentences.zh: 克東安，追破之新寧。

translations.literal: He captured Dong'an and pursued and defeated the bandits at Xinning.
translations.idiomatic: He took Dong'an and pursued the rebels to Xinning, where he routed them.

sentences.zh: 六年，复郴州，擢道員。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he recovered Chenzhou and was promoted to Circuit Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he recovered Chenzhou and was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 江西賊方熾，秉章奏以長佑率蕭啟江等諸軍赴援，克萍鄉，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: The bandits in Jiangxi were then raging; Bingzhang memorialized that Zhangyou should lead the armies of Xiao Qijiang and others to reinforce the province; he captured Pingxiang and was given the rank of Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: With the rebellion in Jiangxi then at its height, Luo Bingzhang memorialized the throne to send Liu Zhangyou at the head of Xiao Qijiang's forces and other units to the rescue; he captured Pingxiang and was granted the rank of surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遣啟江复萬載，進圍袁州，屢擊敗援賊。

translations.literal: He sent Qijiang to recover Wanzai, advanced to besiege Yuanzhou, and repeatedly defeated relieving bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Xiao Qijiang to recover Wanzai, then advanced to besiege Yuanzhou and repeatedly repulsed rebel relief columns.

sentences.zh: 十一月，降賊李能通為內應，克袁州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the surrendered bandit Li Nengtong acted as an inside collaborator, and Yuanzhou was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, the surrendered rebel Li Nengtong turned informer from within, and Yuanzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，進屯太平墟。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, he advanced and encamped at Taipingxu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year, he advanced and encamped at Taiping Market.

sentences.zh: 賊由吉安大舉來襲，列陣二十餘裡，以驍騎衝突，將士多死亡，全軍敗潰。

translations.literal: The bandits came from Ji'an in great force to attack; they drew up their battle lines for more than twenty li, charged with fierce cavalry, many officers and soldiers were killed, and the whole army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels marched out of Ji'an in overwhelming strength; their battle line stretched more than twenty li, and their crack cavalry smashed through the ranks; many officers and men were killed, and the entire army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 長佑下馬引佩刀欲自裁，營務處劉坤一擁之上馬，退保分宜。

translations.literal: Zhangyou dismounted, drew his sword from his belt, and was about to kill himself; Liu Kunyi of the headquarters staff seized him and helped him back onto his horse; they withdrew to defend Fenyi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhangyou dismounted, drew the sword at his belt, and was on the point of taking his own life when Liu Kunyi of the headquarters staff pulled him back onto his horse; they fell back to hold Fenyi.

sentences.zh: 近縣士民爭運糧械濟之，潰卒皆來歸，軍勢復振。

translations.literal: Gentry and common people of the nearby counties vied to transport grain and weapons to supply him; the scattered soldiers all returned, and the army's strength was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners in the neighboring counties rushed forward with grain and arms; the scattered troops rallied to him, and his army recovered its fighting strength.

sentences.zh: 進規臨江，八月，石達開自撫州率二十萬眾來援，總兵普承堯戰峽江不利，賊薄太平墟。

translations.literal: He advanced to threaten Linjiang; in the eighth month, Shi Dakai came from Fuzhou with two hundred thousand men to reinforce the rebels; the Regional Commander Pu Chengyao fought unfavorably at Xiajiang, and the bandits pressed close to Taipingxu.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved against Linjiang; in the eighth month, Shi Dakai marched from Fuzhou with two hundred thousand men to relieve the rebels; Regional Commander Pu Chengyao was defeated at Xiajiang, and the enemy pressed upon Taiping Market.

sentences.zh: 長佑乘其營壘未定，約蕭啟江、田興恕合戰，江忠義、李明惠先陷陣，盧秀峰繞其後，縱擊，大破之，遂圍郡城。

translations.literal: Zhangyou, while their camps and fortifications were not yet settled, arranged with Xiao Qijiang and Tian Xingshu for a joint battle; Jiang Zhongyi and Li Minghui first broke into the enemy lines, Lu Xiufeng circled behind them, and they were released to strike; a great defeat was inflicted, and the commandery seat was then besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Before the enemy camps were fully established, Liu Zhangyou coordinated a joint attack with Xiao Qijiang and Tian Xingshu; Jiang Zhongyi and Li Minghui led the charge into the enemy line, Lu Xiufeng swung around to their rear, and a devastating blow was delivered; the prefectural city was then put under siege.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔嘉其奮勇，賜號齊普圖巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When news of the victory arrived, an edict praised his valor and bestowed upon him the title Qipitu Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the victory reached the court, an edict commended his valor and conferred upon him the title Qipitu Batulu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，克臨江，殲賊酋張發紀，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Linjiang was captured and the bandit chieftain Zhang Faji was exterminated; he was given the rank of Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Linjiang was taken and the rebel chieftain Zhang Faji was killed; Liu Zhangyou was granted the rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年，長佑病歸，以劉坤一代統其眾，蕭啟江自為一軍，合克新淦、崇仁，進克撫州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Zhangyou fell ill and returned home; Liu Kunyi was appointed to take command of his forces in his stead; Xiao Qijiang commanded an army of his own; together they captured Xingan and Chongren and advanced to capture Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Liu Zhangyou fell ill and went home; Liu Kunyi was put in command of his troops, while Xiao Qijiang led a separate force; together they took Xingan and Chongren and went on to capture Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，長佑復至軍，屯建昌，迭敗賊於新城、金谿，敗入福建界。

translations.literal: That summer, Zhangyou returned to the army, encamped at Jianchang, repeatedly defeated the bandits at Xincheng and Jinxi, and drove them into the border of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Liu Zhangyou returned to the field, encamped at Jianchang, repeatedly defeated the rebels at Xincheng and Jinxi, and drove them across the border into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 江西邊境肅清，記名遇江西道員缺簡放。

translations.literal: The Jiangxi border was cleared; he was placed on the register for appointment and, when a Jiangxi circuit intendant vacancy occurred, was selected and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jiangxi frontier had been cleared, he was entered on the register for appointment and, when a Jiangxi circuit intendant post fell vacant, was selected and appointed.

sentences.zh: 九年，回軍湖南剿郴、桂賊，解永州圍，記名以按察使題奏。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he returned his army to Hunan to suppress the bandits in Chen and Gui, lifted the siege of Yongzhou, and was memorialized for appointment as Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, he brought his army back to Hunan to suppress the rebels in Chenzhou and Guilin Prefecture, relieved the siege of Yongzhou, and was recommended for appointment as surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 石達開圍寶慶，長佑與李續宜分扼東西兩路，賊敗走，長佑追破之九鞏橋、白楊埔、大臨橋、蘆洪司，遂竄廣西，陷興安、靈州，直撲桂林。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai besieged Baoqing; Zhangyou and Li Xuyi blocked the eastern and western routes respectively; the bandits were defeated and fled; Zhangyou pursued and defeated them at Jiugong Bridge, Baiyangpu, Dalin Bridge, and Luhongsi; they then fled into Guangxi, captured Xing'an and Lingzhou, and drove straight upon Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai besieged Baoqing, Liu Zhangyou and Li Xuyi blocked the eastern and western approaches respectively; the rebels were routed and fled; Liu Zhangyou pursued and crushed them at Jiugong Bridge, Baiyangpu, Dalin Bridge, and Luhongsi; they then broke into Guangxi, seized Xing'an and Lingzhou, and marched straight on Guilin.

sentences.zh: 長佑倍道赴援，賊不虞其驟至，走慶遠，追擊之，所向皆捷，授廣西按察使，踰月，擢布政使。

translations.literal: Zhangyou marched by forced stages to reinforce the city; the bandits did not expect his sudden arrival and fled to Qingyuan; he pursued and attacked them, and wherever he went he was victorious; he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Guangxi, and within a month was promoted to Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhangyou forced his march to relieve the city; the rebels, not expecting so sudden an arrival, fled to Qingyuan; he pursued and struck them, winning victory after victory; he was appointed surveillance commissioner of Guangxi and, within a month, was promoted to provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 攻柳州，拔之。

translations.literal: He attacked Liuzhou and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Liuzhou and took it.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was promoted to Governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 四月，克慶遠，破達開於思恩，又破之興安，乃遁竄。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Qingyuan was captured; Dakai was defeated at Si'en and again defeated at Xing'an, and then fled in flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Qingyuan was taken; Shi Dakai was defeated at Si'en and routed again at Xing'an, after which he fled.

sentences.zh: 時廣西土匪猶蔓延，大者踞郡縣，小者千百為群，倏兵倏賊。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits in Guangxi still spread far and wide; the larger groups occupied prefectures and counties, the smaller ones gathered in bands of hundreds or thousands, now soldiers, now bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At that time banditry still raged across Guangxi; the larger bands held prefectures and counties, while smaller groups of hundreds or thousands shifted at will between soldiering and brigandage.

sentences.zh: 長佑蒞任，整飭吏治，興練水師，匪氛漸戢。

translations.literal: When Zhangyou took office, he rectified official administration and raised a riverine force; the bandit atmosphere gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office, Liu Zhangyou tightened local administration and built up a riverine force; the scourge of banditry gradually abated.

sentences.zh: 商貨流通，稅釐增倍。

translations.literal: Commercial goods circulated, and tax levies doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Trade flowed freely again, and tax receipts doubled.

sentences.zh: 軍事餉事差能自固，不盡仰資鄰省。

translations.literal: Military affairs and supplies were able to sustain themselves fairly well and did not wholly depend on neighboring provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Military operations and supplies were largely self-sustaining and no longer depended entirely on neighboring provinces.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遣劉坤一剿柳州土匪，斬其渠伍聲揚，餘黨就撫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he dispatched Liu Kunyi to suppress the bandits in Liuzhou, beheaded their leader Wu Shengyang, and the remaining followers submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, he sent Liu Kunyi to suppress the bandits in Liuzhou, had their leader Wu Shengyang executed, and the remaining followers accepted pacification.

sentences.zh: 調水陸軍剿潯州艇匪，克府城，斬其渠陳開。

translations.literal: He transferred land and river forces to suppress the boat bandits at Xunzhou, captured the prefectural seat, and beheaded their leader Chen Kai.
translations.idiomatic: He deployed combined land and river forces against the boat bandits at Xunzhou, took the prefectural city, and executed their leader Chen Kai.

sentences.zh: 貴州匪首黃金義投誠复叛，擒斬之。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Huang Jinyi of Guizhou surrendered and then rebelled again; he was captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jinyi, a bandit chieftain from Guizhou, surrendered and then rebelled again; he was captured and put to death.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，長佑親赴潯州督防，分軍進剿，迭克要隘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Zhangyou personally went to Xunzhou to supervise defense, divided his army to advance in suppression, and repeatedly captured strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign, Liu Zhangyou went in person to Xunzhou to direct the defenses, sent columns forward in pursuit, and captured one strategic pass after another.

sentences.zh: 尋擢兩廣總督，以所部楚軍付劉坤一接統，留剿廣西諸匪。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Governor-General of Liangguang; he handed his Chu army over to Liu Kunyi to take command and remained to suppress the various bandits of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Guangs; he transferred command of his Hunan army to Liu Kunyi and remained behind to suppress the remaining bandits in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，調直隸總督。

translations.literal: Before long, he was transferred to Governor-General of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was transferred to governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 時降捻張錫珠、宋景詩先後叛，畿輔騷動。

translations.literal: At that time the surrendered Nian bandits Zhang Xizhu and Song Jingshi rebelled in succession, and the capital region was thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the surrendered Nian rebels Zhang Xizhu and Song Jingshi rose in succession, throwing the capital region into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 二年春，長佑航海至天津，即赴衡水督師。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, Zhangyou sailed to Tianjin and immediately went to Hengshui to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year, Liu Zhangyou sailed to Tianjin and at once proceeded to Hengshui to take command in the field.

sentences.zh: 三月，破賊束鹿，殲張錫珠。

translations.literal: In the third month, he defeated the bandits at Shulu and exterminated Zhang Xizhu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, he defeated the rebels at Shulu and killed Zhang Xizhu.

sentences.zh: 命督辦直隸、山東、河南三省交界剿匪事宜。

translations.literal: He was ordered to supervise the suppression of bandits in the border regions where Zhili, Shandong, and Henan met.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take charge of suppressing banditry in the borderlands where Zhili, Shandong, and Henan adjoined one another.

sentences.zh: 宋景詩踞劉貫寨、甘官屯，合山東軍攻之，以遲延降級留任。

translations.literal: Song Jingshi occupied Liuguanzhai and Ganguantun; he joined with the Shandong army in attacking them, and because of delay was demoted in rank but retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jingshi held Liuguanzhai and Ganguantun; Liu Zhangyou combined with the Shandong forces to attack him, but because of delays in the campaign was demoted one rank while kept in his post.

sentences.zh: 九月，破賊張秋鎮，殲賊目楊殿一，景詩逸走，乃罷軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, they broke the bandits at Zhangqiu Town, destroyed the bandit chieftain Yang Dianyi, Jing Shi fled, and then the army was disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they routed the rebels at Zhangqiu, killed the bandit leader Yang Dianyi, and Song Jingshi fled the field; the campaign was then brought to a close.

sentences.zh: 四年，僧格林沁戰歿曹州，捻匪益熾，畿南戒嚴，長佑遣兵自開州至張秋扼河防。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Sengge Rinchen died in battle at Caozhou; the Nian bandits burned ever hotter; the region south of the capital was placed on alert; Zhangyou sent troops from Kaizhou to Zhangqiu to choke the river defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Sengge Rinchen fell at Caozhou, the Nian rebellion flared anew, and martial law was declared south of the capital. Liu Zhangyou dispatched troops from Kaizhou to Zhangqiu to hold the river line.

sentences.zh: 奉天馬賊入喜峰口，坐疏防議處。

translations.literal: Fengtian horse bandits entered Xifeng Pass; he was punished by deliberation for lax defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengtian mounted bandits broke through Xifeng Pass, he was censured and disciplined for negligent defense.

sentences.zh: 八月，捻匪竄山東濮、範南岸，長佑馳赴大名，擊走之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Nian bandits fled to the south bank of Pu and Fan in Shandong; Zhangyou galloped to Daming and struck them away.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Nian raiders slipped onto the southern banks of the Pu and Fan in Shandong. Liu Zhangyou raced to Daming and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 疏請直隸分練六軍，議定營製，加練二軍，下部議行。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that Zhili separately drill six armies; camp regulations were fixed; two more armies were added to the drill; the matter was sent down to the ministry for deliberation and execution.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial asking that Zhili be divided into six separately trained armies, with camp organization formally set and two additional armies added to the training scheme; the proposal was referred to the ministry for approval and implementation.

sentences.zh: 六年，滄州梟匪張六等劫慶雲、鹽山、寧津、南皮四縣鹽場，山東教匪應之，保定、天津、河間三府屬皆騷動。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Cangzhou salt-smuggling bandit Zhang Liu and others plundered the salt fields of four counties—Qingyun, Yanshan, Ningjin, and Nanpi; Shandong religious bandits answered them; the jurisdictions under the three prefectures of Baoding, Tianjin, and Hejian were all disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Cangzhou salt lord Zhang Liu and his men raided the salt works of Qingyun, Yanshan, Ningjin, and Nanpi; Shandong sectarian rebels rose in support, and the districts of Baoding, Tianjin, and Hejian were thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 長佑檄前籓司唐訓方屯齊河，臬司張樹聲屯張秋，防捻。

translations.literal: Zhangyou ordered the former provincial treasurer Tang Xunfang to encamp at Qihe and the provincial judge Zhang Shusheng to encamp at Zhangqiu, to guard against the Nian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhangyou directed the former provincial treasurer Tang Xunfang to hold Qihe and the provincial judge Zhang Shusheng to hold Zhangqiu against the Nian.

sentences.zh: 自率兵剿捕鹽梟，賊乘虛北走，過滹沱河，眾增至千餘，竄擾涿州、固安、永清、霸州，逼近京師，詔褫長佑職，以大學士官文代之。

translations.literal: He personally led troops to suppress and capture the salt smugglers; the bandits seized the opening and fled north, crossed the Hutuo River, their numbers swelling to more than a thousand; they fled and ravaged Zhuozhou, Gu'an, Yongqing, and Bazhou, pressing close to the capital; an edict stripped Zhangyou of his office and replaced him with Grand Secretary Guanwen.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the pursuit himself, he moved against the salt smugglers—but the rebels slipped north through the gap, crossed the Hutuo, swelled to more than a thousand men, and ravaged Zhuozhou, Gu'an, Yongqing, and Bazhou until they were almost at the capital's gates. An imperial edict removed Liu Zhangyou from office and appointed Grand Secretary Guanwen in his place.

sentences.zh: 命下數日而梟匪平，予三品頂戴，率所部回籍。

translations.literal: Within days of the order's descent the salt-smuggling bandits were pacified; he was granted a third-rank official's hat button and led his command back to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Only days after the edict was issued the salt lords were subdued. He was granted a third-rank insignia and sent home at the head of his troops.

sentences.zh: 尋東捻平，詔念前勞，晉二品頂戴。

translations.literal: Soon after, the Eastern Nian were pacified; an edict remembered his former labors and promoted him to a second-rank hat button.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Nian were finally crushed, the throne recalled his earlier service and raised him to second-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 十年，起授廣東巡撫，尋調廣西。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was recalled and appointed Governor of Guangdong; soon he was transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was restored to office as Governor of Guangdong, then shortly transferred to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 初，奸民出關劫掠越南，官兵不能制。

translations.literal: At first, wicked commoners crossed the border to plunder Vietnam, and government troops could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: At first, outlaws from within the frontier slipped across the border to raid Vietnam, and the regular troops proved unable to stop them.

sentences.zh: 悍酋吳終伏誅，而蘇國漢復起。

translations.literal: The fierce chieftain Wu Zhong finally submitted to execution, but Su Guohan rose again.
translations.idiomatic: The brutal chieftain Wu Zhong was at last put to death, yet Su Guohan rose in his place.

sentences.zh: 九年，廣西提督馮子材進軍龍州，國漢旋乞撫於兩廣總督瑞麟，仍招納亡命，匪首鄧建新、曾亞日，分路肆擾。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Guangxi Military Governor Feng Zicai advanced on Longzhou; Guohan soon begged pacification from the Governor-General of the Two Guangs, Ruilin, yet still recruited fugitives; bandit chiefs Deng Jianxin and Zeng Yari, along separate routes, ran wild in plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Guangxi Military Governor Feng Zicai marched on Longzhou. Guohan soon sued for peace with Governor-General Ruilin of the Two Guangs, but continued to gather desperadoes; the bandit leaders Deng Jianxin and Zeng Yari split their forces and pillaged at will.

sentences.zh: 至是總兵劉玉成擒亞日於上林社，誅之。

translations.literal: At this time Major General Liu Yucheng captured Yari at Shanglinshe and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Major General Liu Yucheng had seized Yari at Shanglinshe and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 復會廣東軍攻克舊街，乘勝抵海寧，匪多散亡，國漢奔東興，亦就擒。

translations.literal: Again joining Guangdong forces, he captured Jiujie; riding the victory he reached Haing; many bandits scattered and perished; Guohan fled to Dongxing and was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Guangdong troops to take Jiujie, pressed the advantage to Haing, and broke the rebels so thoroughly that most scattered and fled. Guohan fled toward Dongxing and was captured there as well.

sentences.zh: 長佑奏言：「論越南大局，則宜直搗河陽，一勞永逸。

translations.literal: Zhangyou memorialized, saying: "When discussing the great situation of Vietnam, one ought to strike directly at Heyang, one labor and forever ease.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhangyou memorialized the throne: "If we mean to settle Vietnam's larger troubles, we should strike straight at Heyang and be done with it once and for all.

sentences.zh: 然河陽距關二千餘裡，窮兵勞費，討捕為難​​。

translations.literal: Yet Heyang is more than two thousand li from the pass; exhausting the army would be costly; pursuit and capture would be hard.
translations.idiomatic: But Heyang lies more than two thousand li beyond the border. To drive the army that far would drain men and money, and the rebels would be hard to run down.

sentences.zh: 今擬芟盪海陽、太原，即回師列戍，以固籓籬。

translations.literal: Now we plan to sweep clean Haiyang and Taiyuan, then withdraw the army and array garrisons to solidify the vassal fence.
translations.idiomatic: Our present plan is to scour Haiyang and Taiyuan, then pull back and station troops along the line to shore up the frontier buffer.

sentences.zh: 庶可分助越之眾，協剿黔苗；

translations.literal: Thus we may divide and assist Vietnam's forces, jointly suppressing the Miao of Guizhou;
translations.idiomatic: In that way we can spare part of our strength to aid the Vietnamese while joining the campaign against the Miao in Guizhou;

sentences.zh: 抽出關之兵，先清土莽。」

translations.literal: and withdraw troops from the pass to first clear the local bandits."
translations.idiomatic: and redeploy border troops to sweep the hill country clean first."

sentences.zh: 十月，副將陳得貴、游擊李揚才克越南從化府，遂會劉玉成克通化、白通，破瓊山、北山匪巢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Deputy General Chen Degui and Colonel Li Yangcai captured Vietnam's Cong Hoa Prefecture; then they joined Liu Yucheng to capture Tong Hoa and Bach Thong, and broke the bandit nests of Khuong Son and Bac Son.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Deputy General Chen Degui and Colonel Li Yangcai took Vietnam's Cong Hoa Prefecture, then joined Liu Yucheng to seize Tong Hoa and Bach Thong and destroy the rebel strongholds in the Khuong Son and Bac Son ranges.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，复敗匪於三星山，擒其酋何三等，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, they again defeated the bandits at Sanxing Mountain, captured their chieftain He San and others, and all remaining followers were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year they routed the rebels again at Sanxing Mountain, captured the chieftain He San and his lieutenants, and wiped out the last of the band.

sentences.zh: 長佑檄劉玉成暫屯鎮撫，諮越南國王遣兵換防，久之不至；

translations.literal: Zhangyou ordered Liu Yucheng to encamp temporarily for pacification, and consulted the King of Vietnam to send troops to relieve the garrison; after a long time they did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhangyou kept Liu Yucheng in place to hold and pacify the region and asked the Vietnamese king to send troops to relieve them—but the relief never came.

sentences.zh: 又以營弁滋事，暴兵非計，七月，乃撤入關內，搜捕沿邊伏匪。

translations.literal: Also, because officers were causing trouble, keeping troops deployed by force was not a plan; in the seventh month he therefore withdrew into the interior of the pass and searched out hidden bandits along the border.
translations.idiomatic: Officers were also stirring up trouble, and leaving troops abroad by main force was no solution. In the seventh month he pulled back inside the pass and hunted down hidden rebels along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 時匪酋黃崇英猶踞越南河陽，結白苗攻保樂，擾我鎮安邊。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chieftain Huang Chongying still occupied Heyang in Vietnam, allied with the White Miao to attack Bao Le, and harassed our Zhen'an border.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the bandit chief Huang Chongying still held Heyang in Vietnam, joined the White Miao in an assault on Bao Le, and raided our Zhen'an frontier.

sentences.zh: 十二年春，長佑檄關內外軍擊走之，密奏：「越南貧弱，版章日蹙，法國蠶食於濱海，黎裔虎視於橫山，桶岡則白苗跳梁，峒奔則黃酋雄踞。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year, Zhangyou ordered troops inside and outside the pass to strike them away, and secretly memorialized: "Vietnam is poor and weak; its territory daily narrows; France nibbles at the coast; the Li heritage watches like tigers from Hengshan; at Tonggang the White Miao leap about in disorder; at Dongben the Yellow chieftain holds dominion.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twelfth year Liu Zhangyou sent troops on both sides of the pass to drive them off and submitted a confidential memorial: "Vietnam grows ever poorer and weaker, its domain shrinking day by day. France gnaws at the coast. The Li faction watches from Hengshan like tigers at prey. At Tonggang the White Miao run riot; at Dongben Huang's chieftain sits enthroned in defiance.

sentences.zh: 近聞其國君臣輸款法人，黃崇英受職黎裔，雖係道聽之言，亦係意中之事。

translations.literal: Recently I heard that their king and ministers have submitted allegiance to the French, and Huang Chongying has received office from the Li heritage; though this is hearsay on the road, it is also a matter within expectation.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately heard that the Vietnamese court is treating with the French and that Huang Chongying has taken office under the Li faction. It may be nothing but camp gossip—but it is exactly the sort of thing one would expect.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂黎裔為患，越南受之；

translations.literal: Your minister ventures to say: if the Li heritage becomes a calamity, Vietnam will receive it;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes that if the Li faction becomes a threat, Vietnam alone will suffer it;

sentences.zh: 法國為患，不僅越南受之。

translations.literal: if France becomes a calamity, not only Vietnam will receive it.
translations.idiomatic: but if France becomes a threat, Vietnam will not be the only one to suffer.

sentences.zh: 今欲拯敝扶衰，必須大舉深入。

translations.literal: Now, if we wish to save the worn and support the failing, we must mount a great campaign and go deep.
translations.idiomatic: If we mean to rescue a realm already near collapse, we must commit ourselves to a major advance deep into their country.

sentences.zh: 若合兩粵之力，寬以數年之期，步步設防，節節進剿，庶交夷可期復振，而他族不至生心。

translations.literal: If we combine the strength of the Two Guangs, grant the span of several years, establish defenses step by step, and advance suppression joint by joint, then perhaps the neighboring barbarians may be expected to revive, and other peoples will not come to harbor designs.
translations.idiomatic: With the Two Guangs united, given several years, defenses set at each stage and offensives pressed from one strongpoint to the next, the neighboring kingdom might yet be restored—and other powers might think twice before moving against us.

sentences.zh: 否則惟有慎固邊防，嚴杜勾結而已。」

translations.literal: Otherwise there is only carefully securing the border defenses and strictly blocking collusion."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise our only course is to tighten the frontier and cut off every channel of collusion."

sentences.zh: 是時防越諸軍尚八千人，長佑檄劉玉成引軍北還，以六營屯關外諸隘，四營屯歸順、龍卅，令覃遠璡八營分駐關內。

translations.literal: At that time the armies defending Vietnam still numbered eight thousand; Zhangyou ordered Liu Yucheng to lead the army north back; six battalions were stationed at the passes outside the border; four battalions were stationed at Guishun and Longzhou; Tan Yuanjin's eight battalions were ordered to garrison separately inside the pass."
translations.idiomatic: At that time eight thousand men still guarded the Vietnamese frontier. Liu Zhangyou recalled Liu Yucheng to the north, left six battalions at the outer passes, four at Guishun and Longzhou, and posted Tan Yuanjin's eight battalions at stations inside the border.

sentences.zh: 十月，法人攻陷河內，黃崇英等乘機襲太原，潛與之通。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the French captured Hanoi; Huang Chongying and others seized the opportunity to raid Taiyuan and secretly communicated with them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the French took Hanoi. Huang Chongying and his men seized the moment to strike at Taiyuan, secretly treating with the invaders.

sentences.zh: 山西奸民響應，北寧戒嚴。

translations.literal: Wicked commoners in Son Tay responded; Bac Ninh was placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Local ruffians in Son Tay rose in support, and Bac Ninh was put under martial alert.

sentences.zh: 越南乞援，乃令劉玉成統十營進太原為左軍，道員趙沃統十營分部鎮安為右軍。

translations.literal: Vietnam begged for aid; then Liu Yucheng was ordered to command ten battalions advancing on Taiyuan as the Left Army, and Circuit Intendant Zhao Wo to command ten battalions distributed at Zhen'an as the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: Vietnam appealed for help. Liu Yucheng was placed at the head of ten battalions marching on Taiyuan as the Left Army; Circuit Intendant Zhao Wo took ten battalions posted around Zhen'an as the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 法人尋與越南議和，黃崇英為越將劉永福所敗，潛伏河陽，遣黨陳亞水攻保樂。

translations.literal: The French soon made peace with Vietnam; Huang Chongying was defeated by the Vietnamese general Liu Yongfu, went into hiding at Heyang, and sent his follower Chen Yashui to attack Bao Le.
translations.idiomatic: The French soon negotiated peace with Vietnam. Huang Chongying, beaten by the Vietnamese general Liu Yongfu, went to ground at Heyang and sent his lieutenant Chen Yashui against Bao Le.

sentences.zh: 十三年十月，長佑閱兵南寧，令趙沃、劉玉成進軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year, Zhangyou reviewed troops at Nanning and ordered Zhao Wo and Liu Yucheng to advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year Liu Zhangyou inspected the troops at Nanning and ordered Zhao Wo and Liu Yucheng forward.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年二月，趙沃右軍由龍闌渡河克同文，白苗棄巢遁，沃撫之為助，遂攻底定、襄​​安，皆克之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Guangxu, Zhao Wo's Right Army crossed the river at Longlan and captured Dong Van; the White Miao abandoned their nests and fled; Wo pacified them to serve as auxiliaries; then he attacked Dinh Dinh and Tuong An, and both were captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Guangxu, Zhao Wo's Right Army forded the river at Longlan and took Dong Van. The White Miao abandoned their camps and fled; Zhao Wo won them over as allies, then carried Dinh Dinh and Tuong An in succession.

sentences.zh: 劉玉成左軍敗賊白通，陣斬鄧志雄。

translations.literal: Liu Yucheng's Left Army defeated the bandits at Bach Thong and beheaded Deng Zhixiong in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yucheng's Left Army broke the rebels at Bach Thong and killed Deng Zhixiong on the field.

sentences.zh: 崇英聞師至，嗾周建新拒左軍，陳亞水守猛法，自當右軍，憑險拒守。

translations.literal: When Chongying heard the army had arrived, he incited Zhou Jianxin to block the Left Army, had Chen Yashui hold Mong Phap, and personally faced the Right Army, relying on dangerous terrain to resist and hold.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongying learned the imperial columns were closing in, he set Zhou Jianxin to stop the Left Army, put Chen Yashui in charge of Mong Phap, and took the Right Army on himself, fighting from the high ground.

sentences.zh: 五月，沃軍克淰台，直薄河陽，崇英敗走。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Wo's army captured Dam Thai and pressed directly on Heyang; Chongying was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhao Wo's force took Dam Thai and bore straight down on Heyang. Chongying broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 右軍复敗陸之平援眾，進攻猛法。

translations.literal: The Right Army again defeated Lu Zhiping's relief force and advanced to attack Mong Phap.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Army then routed Lu Zhiping's relief column and pushed on against Mong Phap.

sentences.zh: 陳亞水惶懼，乞為內應，河陽、安邊同日降。

translations.literal: Chen Yashui, in fear and panic, begged to serve as an inside agent; Heyang and An Bien surrendered on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Chen Yashui offered to open the gates from within. Heyang and An Bien fell the same day.

sentences.zh: 崇英遁走，捕獲誅之。

translations.literal: Chongying fled in escape, was captured, and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Chongying fled, was run down, captured, and executed.

sentences.zh: 劉玉成左軍亦克通化、白通，斬周建新，合攻者岩，克之。

translations.literal: Liu Yucheng's Left Army also captured Tong Hoa and Bach Thong, beheaded Zhou Jianxin, jointly attacked Gia Nham, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yucheng's Left Army likewise took Tong Hoa and Bach Thong, cut off Zhou Jianxin's head, and joined the assault on Gia Nham until it too fell.

sentences.zh: 陸之平遁，宣光、金沙江上下肅清。

translations.literal: Lu Zhiping fled; Xuanguang and the upper and lower reaches of the Golden Sand River were cleared and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhiping escaped. Xuanguang and the length of the Golden Sand River were swept clean.

sentences.zh: 凱撤入關。

translations.literal: In triumph he withdrew into the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Victorious, he marched back through the pass.

sentences.zh: 擢雲貴總督，二年，抵任。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou; in the second year he arrived to assume office.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou, and took up the post in the second year.

sentences.zh: 先是，滇邊野番殺英人馬加理，為交涉鉅案，及議定，允於雲南設埠通商。

translations.literal: Previously, wild tribes on the Yunnan frontier killed the Englishman Margary; it became a major diplomatic case, and once negotiations were settled, permission was granted to establish a treaty port in Yunnan for trade.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, wild tribes on the Yunnan border had killed the British agent Augustus Margary in the Margary Affair; after negotiations the court agreed to open a treaty port in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 詔下其議，長佑疏言：「雲南山川深阻，種人獷悍成性，剽掠行旅。

translations.literal: An edict issued this decision; Zhangyou memorialized, saying: "Yunnan's mountains and rivers are deep and obstructive; the tribal peoples are wild and fierce by nature, and plunder travelers.
translations.idiomatic: The decision was promulgated by edict. Liu Zhangyou memorialized: "Yunnan's mountains are steep and its rivers forbidding; the native peoples are fierce by habit and prey on travelers.

sentences.zh: 本地紳練，恃眾橫行，挾制官長。

translations.literal: Local gentry militia, relying on their numbers, act lawlessly and coerce the officials.
translations.idiomatic: The local gentry militia swagger about in numbers and hold their superiors hostage to their will.

sentences.zh: 上下猜忌，法令不行。

translations.literal: High and low mutually suspect one another, and laws and orders are not enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people distrust one another, and the law cannot be enforced.

sentences.zh: 萬一防護不及，致有同於前案，或更甚於前案，其有害於雲南一隅猶小，其有撓於中夏全局甚大。

translations.literal: If protection should prove insufficient and there occur events like the previous case, or even worse than the previous case, the harm to one corner of Yunnan would still be small, but the injury to the entire Central Realm would be very great.
translations.idiomatic: If protection falls short and another Margary Affair—or worse—should follow, the damage to one corner of Yunnan would be small compared with the blow to the empire as a whole.

sentences.zh: 且洋人知前案難辦，有免其既往之議；

translations.literal: Moreover, the Westerners, knowing the previous case was hard to handle, had proposals to exempt what was past;
translations.idiomatic: The foreigners, knowing the earlier case could not easily be pursued, proposed to let bygones be bygones;

sentences.zh: 知後患難防，有保其將來之議。

translations.literal: knowing that future trouble was hard to guard against, had proposals to guarantee what was to come.
translations.idiomatic: knowing future trouble would be hard to prevent, proposed guarantees for the time to come.

sentences.zh: 臣恐滇省官民，於已往者不以為倖免，而以為得計；

translations.literal: Your minister fears that officials and people of Yunnan Province, regarding what is past, will not take it as a lucky escape but will take it as a successful stratagem;
translations.idiomatic: I fear the officials and people of Yunnan will not regard the pardon of past offenses as a lucky escape, but as a winning scheme;

sentences.zh: 將來者不引為前鑑，或敢於效尤。

translations.literal: regarding what is to come, will not take it as a warning from the past, and may dare to follow the bad example.
translations.idiomatic: and that rather than learn from it, they may dare to repeat the offense.

sentences.zh: 洋人通商，意在圖利，亦斷無不思遠害之理。

translations.literal: Westerners in trade seek profit; it also cannot be that they do not reason about keeping harm far away.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign traders seek profit—but they surely also wish to keep trouble at a distance.

sentences.zh: 應俟三五年內外官民稍稍安定，遣員商辦。」

translations.literal: One ought to wait three to five years until officials and people within and without are somewhat settled, then send an officer to negotiate the arrangements."
translations.idiomatic: We should wait three to five years until officials and people on both sides have settled down somewhat, then send a commissioner to negotiate trade."

sentences.zh: 長佑以滇事漸定，屢疏引病乞罷，優詔慰留。

translations.literal: As Yunnan affairs gradually settled, Zhangyou repeatedly memorialized citing illness to beg dismissal; gracious edicts comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: As Yunnan affairs gradually quieted, Liu Zhangyou repeatedly begged leave on grounds of illness; the throne answered with gracious edicts urging him to stay.

sentences.zh: 四年，騰越徼外土目耿榮高等攻陷耿馬，長佑遣將討之，榮高降；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, beyond the frontier at Tengyue the local chieftain Geng Ronggao and others attacked and captured Gengma; Zhangyou sent a general to suppress them, and Ronggao surrendered;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the native chieftain Geng Ronggao and others beyond the Tengyue frontier stormed Gengma; Liu Zhangyou sent a general against them and Ronggao surrendered.

sentences.zh: 又剿平臨安、開化、廣南土匪。

translations.literal: He also suppressed and pacified the bandits of Lin'an, Kaihua, and Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He also wiped out the bandits of Lin'an, Kaihua, and Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 初，騰越蘇關先之亂，其黨劉寶玉逃之野山。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the uprising of Su Guanxian at Tengyue, his follower Liu Baoyu fled to the Wild Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: During an earlier revolt by Su Guanxian at Tengyue, his follower Liu Baoyu had fled into the Wild Mountains.

sentences.zh: 野山在滇、緬之交，其夷自為君長，不隸羈屬。

translations.literal: The Wild Mountains lie at the junction of Yunnan and Burma; there the barbarians have their own rulers and are subject to no binding jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: The Wild Mountains lay where Yunnan met Burma; the tribes there acknowledged their own chiefs and owed allegiance to no outside power.

sentences.zh: 劉寶玉糾野貫十三種及盞達夷伏羅坤山，時出劫掠。

translations.literal: Liu Baoyu gathered the thirteen Ye Guan tribes and the Zhanda Yi, concealed themselves on Luokun Mountain, and from time to time emerged to raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Baoyu rallied the thirteen Ye Guan tribes and the Zhanda Yi, lurked on Luokun Mountain, and sallied forth to raid whenever opportunity offered.

sentences.zh: 會緬甸遣官詣騰越，持圖說約由野山通道列戍。

translations.literal: At that time Burma sent an official to Tengyue, holding maps and proposals to garrison the route through the Wild Mountains pass.
translations.idiomatic: About then Burma sent an envoy to Tengyue with maps proposing to garrison a route through the Wild Mountains.

sentences.zh: 長佑檄熊昭鏡赴騰越，召諸土司、野貫申禁約，誘誅寶玉於千崖，諸野夷皆解散。

translations.literal: Zhangyou ordered Xiong Zhaojing to go to Tengyue, summoned the various native chiefs and Ye Guan to announce prohibitions and covenants, lured and executed Baoyu at Qianya, and all the wild tribes dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhangyou ordered Xiong Zhaojing to Tengyue, summoned the native chiefs and Ye Guan to renew the ban, lured Liu Baoyu out and had him killed at Qianya, and the wild tribes all scattered.

sentences.zh: 七年，法兵窺越南東京，詔滇、粵備邊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, French troops watched covetously toward Tonkin in Vietnam; an edict ordered Yunnan and Guangdong to prepare the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year French troops began probing Tonkin; the court ordered Yunnan and Guangdong to ready the border defenses.

sentences.zh: 長佑疏言：「法人自據嘉定以來，越南四境皆有商埠、教堂，脅其君臣，漁其財力。

translations.literal: Zhangyou memorialized, saying: "Since the French have held Gia Dinh, every quarter of Vietnam has had trading ports and churches; they intimidate its ruler and ministers and drain its wealth and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhangyou memorialized: "Since the French seized Gia Dinh, trading ports and churches have sprung up across Vietnam; they intimidate the court and bleed the country dry.

sentences.zh: 取越與否，非有甚異。

translations.literal: Whether or not they take Vietnam, there is no great difference.
translations.idiomatic: Whether they seize Vietnam outright or not makes little real difference.

sentences.zh: 其所以處心積慮，乃在通商雲南。

translations.literal: What they brood over and scheme for lies in opening trade in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: What they have been scheming toward all along is trade access to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 與其既失越境，為守邊之計，不若乘其始動，為弭釁之謀。

translations.literal: Rather than, once Vietnam's territory is already lost, making plans only to defend the border, it would be better, while they have only just begun to move, to adopt a plan to extinguish the quarrel at its source.
translations.idiomatic: Better to strike while they are only beginning to move than to wait until Vietnam is lost and resign ourselves to defending a long frontier.

sentences.zh: 滇、粵三省，與越接壤，東西幾二千里，要害與共，勞費殊甚。

translations.literal: The three provinces of Yunnan, Guangdong, and Guangxi border Vietnam; east to west it is nearly two thousand li; strategic points are shared in common, and labor and expense are extraordinarily heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan, Guangdong, and Guangxi all border Vietnam along nearly two thousand li from east to west; the key points are shared, and the cost of defense would be enormous.

sentences.zh: 若自三江口以至海陽，東西僅數百里，以中國兵力為之禦敵，兵聚而力省。

translations.literal: If from Sanjiangkou to Haiyang, east to west is only several hundred li, using China's military strength to oppose the enemy there, troops would be concentrated and strength conserved.
translations.idiomatic: From Sanjiangkou to Haiyang the front is only a few hundred li across; there China's forces could mass together and meet the enemy at far less cost.

sentences.zh: 以視防守滇、粵邊境，勞逸懸殊。

translations.literal: Compared with defending the Yunnan and Guangdong frontiers, toil and ease are wildly apart.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with holding the long Yunnan and Guangdong border, the difference in effort would be vast.

sentences.zh: 請以廣西兵二萬為中路，廣東、雲南各以萬人相犄角。

translations.literal: He requested that twenty thousand Guangxi troops serve as the center army, with Guangdong and Yunnan each contributing ten thousand men in mutual supporting horns.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed twenty thousand Guangxi troops for the center, with ten thousand each from Guangdong and Yunnan in supporting wings.

sentences.zh: 廣東之兵自欽、連而入，雲南之兵出洮江而東。

translations.literal: Guangdong's troops would enter from Qinzhou and Lianzhou; Yunnan's troops would go east out of the Taojiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong's column would advance from Qinzhou and Lianzhou; Yunnan's would march east from the Red River.

sentences.zh: 別以輪船守廣東順化港口，斷其首尾，法人必無自全之理。」

translations.literal: Separately, with steamships from Guangdong guarding the port of Hue, cutting head from tail, the French would certainly have no means of preserving themselves."
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, steamships from Guangdong could block the port of Hue and cut the enemy's line in two; the French would have no way to save themselves."

sentences.zh: 又力言劉永福可禦敵，請密諭越王給其兵食。

translations.literal: He also strongly argued that Liu Yongfu could resist the enemy and requested a secret instruction to the King of Vietnam to supply his army with provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He also insisted that Liu Yongfu could hold the enemy and asked that the Vietnamese king be secretly instructed to supply his troops.

sentences.zh: 疏入，詔下廷議。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, an edict ordered it sent down for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received and referred to the full court for debate.

sentences.zh: 八年，法兵陷東京，越匪紛起，廣西援兵至太原，長佑檄道員沈壽榕率軍出關，與為聲援。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, French troops captured Tonkin; Vietnamese bandits rose in disorder on all sides; Guangxi relief troops reached Taiyuan; Zhangyou ordered Circuit Intendant Shen Shourong to lead an army out of the pass to lend them support.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the French took Tonkin; rebellion flared across Vietnam; Guangxi relief forces reached Thái Nguyên; Liu Zhangyou ordered Circuit Intendant Shen Shourong to lead troops across the border in support.

sentences.zh: 長佑屢以病乞罷，慰留未許。

translations.literal: Zhangyou repeatedly begged leave on grounds of illness; comforting retention was offered but not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhangyou repeatedly asked to resign on grounds of illness, but the court kept him in place despite its reassuring edicts.

sentences.zh: 八月，入覲，予假兩月，九年，乃許開缺回籍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he came to audience; leave of two months was granted; in the ninth year he was finally permitted to vacate his post and return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he had audience with the emperor and was granted two months' leave; in the ninth year he was at last allowed to surrender his post and return home.

sentences.zh: 尋坐雲南報銷失察，降三級。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was punished for failure to oversee Yunnan's accounts settlement and was demoted three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was demoted three ranks for lax oversight of Yunnan's expense accounts.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 詔念前功，嘉其端謹老成，開復處分，仍依總督例議卹，諡武慎。

translations.literal: An edict recalled his earlier achievements, praised his upright prudence and mature steadiness, restored his penalties, still ordered mourning benefits according to the governor-general precedent, and posthumously named him Wuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his past service and steady character, restored his ranks, granted mourning honors befitting a governor-general, and gave him the posthumous name Wuzhen, "Martial and Cautious."

sentences.zh: 廣西、雲南、湖南並立專祠。

translations.literal: Dedicated temples were jointly established in Guangxi, Yunnan, and Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial shrines were erected to him in Guangxi, Yunnan, and Hunan.

sentences.zh: 劉岳昭，字藎臣，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Liu Yuezhao, courtesy name Jinchen, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuezhao, styled Jinchen, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以文童投效湘軍。

translations.literal: As a young scholar he joined and served the Hunan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hunan Army as a student volunteer.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，從蕭啟江援江西，轉戰積功，累擢以知縣用。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he followed Xiao Qijiang to reinforce Jiangxi, fought in successive campaigns and accumulated merit, and was repeatedly promoted for appointment as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Xianfeng reign he marched with Xiao Qijiang to relieve Jiangxi, won distinction in repeated campaigns, and rose through the ranks toward appointment as county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 啟江器其才，使領果後營。

translations.literal: Qijiang valued his talent and had him command the Guohou Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qijiang, impressed by his ability, put him in command of the Guohou Battalion.

sentences.zh: 七年，破賊高安鶯哥嶺，連拔彭家村賊巢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he defeated the bandits at Yingge Ridge in Gao'an and in succession captured the bandit lairs at Pengjiacun.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he routed the rebels at Yingge Ridge near Gao'an and stormed one bandit stronghold after another at Pengjiacun.

sentences.zh: 進攻臨江，擊敗援賊於太平墟。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Linjiang and defeated relief bandits at Taipingxu.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack on Linjiang and routed the rebel relief force at Taipingxu.

sentences.zh: 尋克臨江府城，擢同知。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he captured the Linjiang prefectural city and was promoted to Sub-Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took the prefectural city of Linjiang and was promoted to sub-prefect.

sentences.zh: 八年，從剿撫州賊，大捷於何家村、香溪諸處。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed in the suppression of the Fuzhou bandits and won a great victory at Hejiacun, Xiangxi, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he took part in the campaign against the rebels at Fuzhou and won major victories at Hejiacun, Xiangxi, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 崇仁賊踞白陂墟，又破之。

translations.literal: The bandits of Chongren held Baipixu; he again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongren rebels held Baipixu, he broke them again.

sentences.zh: 由上頓渡進偪撫州，賊開東門逸，復其城，擢知府，賜花翎。

translations.literal: From Shangdundu he advanced to press Fuzhou; the bandits opened the east gate and escaped; he recovered the city, was promoted to Prefect, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing from Shangdundu he closed on Fuzhou; the rebels slipped out the east gate and fled; he recovered the city, was promoted to prefect, and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 九年，援南康，克新城墟，進搗池江。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he reinforced Nankang, captured Xinchengxu, and advanced to strike Chijiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he relieved Nankang, took Xinchengxu, and pushed on against Chijiang.

sentences.zh: 前軍潰，岳昭殿後，斃賊甚眾，克南安，援信豐，解其圍，加道員銜。

translations.literal: The vanguard was routed; Yuezhao covered the rear, killed very many bandits, captured Nan'an, relieved Xinfeng, lifted its siege, and was given the rank of Circuit Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the vanguard collapsed, Liu Yuezhao held the rear and killed a great many rebels; he took Nan'an, marched to relieve Xinfeng, broke the siege there, and was granted the rank of circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 石達開由江西擁眾犯湖南，岳昭移軍茶陵備之，而賊已趨寶慶，奉檄馳援。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai gathered troops from Jiangxi and invaded Hunan; Yuezhao moved his army to Chaling to prepare against him, but the bandits had already hastened toward Baoqing; he received orders and rushed to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai marched from Jiangxi into Hunan at the head of a large force, Liu Yuezhao shifted his troops to Chaling to block him; but the rebels had already turned toward Baoqing, so he received urgent orders and raced to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 至柳家橋，遏東路，賊六萬餘撲營，岳昭偕副將餘星元、楊恆升等鏖戰三日，斃賊數千，援軍大集，賊解圍而遁。

translations.literal: Reaching Liujia Bridge, he blocked the eastern route; more than sixty thousand bandits stormed the camp; Yuezhao, together with Deputy Generals Yu Xingyuan, Yang Hengsheng, and others, fought fiercely for three days, killed several thousand bandits, relief armies gathered in great numbers, and the bandits lifted the siege and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Liujia Bridge he blocked the eastern approach; more than sixty thousand rebels assaulted his camp. Liu Yuezhao, together with Deputy Generals Yu Xingyuan and Yang Hengsheng and others, fought pitched battles for three days and killed several thousand enemy soldiers. Once relief columns had massed in strength, the rebels broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是役岳昭戰最力，名始顯。

translations.literal: In this battle Yuezhao fought with the greatest exertion, and his name first became prominent.
translations.idiomatic: In this engagement Liu Yuezhao had fought with exceptional vigor, and his reputation began to rise.

sentences.zh: 十年，屯江華，賊酋陳金剛踞廣西​​賀縣，阻山為固，岳昭招降其黨。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he encamped at Jianghua; the bandit chieftain Chen Jingang occupied Hexian in Guangxi, relying on the mountains for defense; Yuezhao induced his followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he encamped at Jianghua. The rebel chieftain Chen Jingang held Hexian in Guangxi, fortified in the mountains; Liu Yuezhao persuaded many of his followers to defect.

sentences.zh: 進拔蓮塘縣，破河東街賊屯，合蔣益澧軍克縣城，以道員記名，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: He advanced to capture Liantang County, destroyed the bandit encampment at Hedong Street, joined Jiang Yili's army to capture the county seat, was placed on the register as a circuit intendant, and was given the rank of Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to take Liantang County, smashed the rebel stronghold at Hedong Street, and together with Jiang Yili's forces captured the county seat; he was placed on the register for appointment as circuit intendant and granted the rank of surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，連破竄匪於道州、宜章，湘境肅清，賜號鼓勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: That winter, he repeatedly defeated fleeing bandits at Daozhou and Yizhang; the Hunan border was cleared; he was bestowed the title Guyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he routed fleeing rebels in succession at Daozhou and Yizhang, clearing the Hunan frontier, and was granted the title Guyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，駱秉章赴四川督師，疏請岳昭率所部從行。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Luo Bingzhang went to Sichuan to supervise the army; he memorialized requesting that Yuezhao lead his own division to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Luo Bingzhang went to Sichuan to take command of the campaign and memorialized the throne asking that Liu Yuezhao bring his own troops with him.

sentences.zh: 中途聞粵匪陳玉成犯湖北，陷隨州，秉章令岳昭回軍赴援，會諸軍克之，以按察使記名。

translations.literal: Midway he heard that the Cantonese bandit Chen Yucheng invaded Hubei and captured Suizhou; Bingzhang ordered Yuezhao to turn his army back to reinforce; together with the various armies he captured it; he was placed on the register as Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: En route he learned that the Cantonese rebel Chen Yucheng had invaded Hubei and taken Suizhou; Luo Bingzhang ordered Liu Yuezhao to turn back and reinforce the province. Joining with the other armies, he recovered the city and was placed on the register for appointment as surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 石達開由龍山犯宣恩，窺伺施南，岳昭迎擊走之。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai came from Longshan to invade Xuan'en, watching for an opportunity at Shinan; Yuezhao met him in attack and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai marched from Longshan against Xuan'en, threatening to strike toward Shinan; Liu Yuezhao met him in battle and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 而黔匪陷來鳳，同治元年春，岳昭進軍克其城，分軍截剿，迭捷於散毛河、白蘭壩兩河口，抵黑洞，斬馘尤多。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Guizhou bandits captured Laifeng; in the spring of the first year of Tongzhi, Yuezhao advanced and captured the city, divided his army to intercept and suppress, achieved repeated victories at Sanmao River, Bailan Dam, and Lianghekou, and reached Heidong; beheadings were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Guizhou rebels had taken Laifeng. In the spring of the first year of Tongzhi, Liu Yuezhao advanced and recovered the city; he sent detachments to cut off and hunt down the enemy, winning successive victories at Sanmao River, Bailan Dam, and Lianghekou, and reaching Heidong, where the toll of enemy dead was especially heavy.

sentences.zh: 石達開竄四川，圍涪州，岳昭會知府唐蜅、副將唐有耕破之仰天窩。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai fled into Sichuan and besieged Fuzhou; Yuezhao joined Prefect Tang Fu and Deputy General Tang Yougeng to defeat him at Yangtiangwo.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai fled into Sichuan and besieged Fuzhou; Liu Yuezhao, together with Prefect Tang Fu and Deputy General Tang Yougeng, defeated him at Yangtiangwo.

sentences.zh: 渡江重慶截擊，解涪州圍。

translations.literal: Crossing the river to Chongqing to intercept, he lifted the siege of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river to Chongqing to intercept the enemy and broke the siege of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊敗踞長寧，攻克之，复追敗之先市寨、得用壩、丁子場。

translations.literal: The bandits, defeated, occupied Changning; he captured it, then again pursued and defeated them at Xianshizhai, Deyongba, and Dingzichang.
translations.idiomatic: The defeated rebels fell back on Changning; he took the city, then pursued and routed them again at Xianshizhai, Deyongba, and Dingzichang.

sentences.zh: 賊尋踞敘州雙龍場，約降賊郭集益內應，破其營，殪賊近二萬。

translations.literal: The bandits soon occupied Shuanglongchang in Xuzhou; he arranged with the surrendered bandit Guo Jiyi for inside collaboration, destroyed their camp, and exterminated nearly twenty thousand bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon occupied Shuanglong Market in Xuzhou; Liu Yuezhao secured the cooperation of the surrendered rebel Guo Jiyi from within, smashed their camp, and killed nearly twenty thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 貴州巡撫張亮基疏薦其才，請擢用，二年，授雲南按察使；

translations.literal: Guizhou Governor Zhang Liangji memorialized recommending his talent and requesting promotion; in the second year he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Yunnan;
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou Governor Zhang Liangji memorialized the throne, commending his ability and asking that he be promoted; in the second year he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Yunnan;

sentences.zh: 三年，遷布政使；

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Provincial Administration Commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner;

sentences.zh: 皆未之任，留四川治軍。

translations.literal: None of these posts did he assume; he remained in Sichuan to manage the army.
translations.idiomatic: He never took up any of these appointments, remaining in Sichuan to command the army.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章奏遣援黔，九月，克仁懷，連敗馬氾灘踞匪。

translations.literal: Luo Bingzhang memorialized dispatching him to reinforce Guizhou; in the ninth month he captured Renhuai and repeatedly defeated bandits entrenched at Maofantan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Bingzhang memorialized for him to be sent to reinforce Guizhou; in the ninth month he took Renhuai and in succession defeated rebels holding Maofantan.

sentences.zh: 四年，克正安，追賊至清溪河，斬其渠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he captured Zheng'an, pursued the bandits to Qingxi River, and beheaded their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he captured Zheng'an, pursued the rebels to Qingxi River, and killed their leader.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢雲南巡撫，進規綏陽。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Governor of Yunnan and advanced to threaten Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was elevated to Governor of Yunnan and moved against Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 天台山最為城北險隘，列陣綴其前，從山後攻入，平其壘，投誠者三百餘寨。

translations.literal: Tiantai Mountain was the most perilous pass north of the city; he drew up his battle lines to hold them in front, attacked from behind the mountain, leveled their fortifications, and more than three hundred stockades submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tiantai Mountain was the most formidable barrier north of the city; he deployed his forces to pin the enemy in front, then attacked from the mountain's rear, overran their fortifications, and more than three hundred stockades came over in submission.

sentences.zh: 綏陽城賊吳元彪乞降，黔西北路始通。

translations.literal: The bandit Wu Yuanbiao in Suiyang city begged to surrender; the northwestern route of Guizhou was finally opened.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanbiao, the rebel holding Suiyang city, petitioned to surrender, and the northwest route through Guizhou was at last clear.

sentences.zh: 由溫水進剿，平菉竹山老巢，收降鐵匠坪、九倉壩及被脅岩洞二十餘處。

translations.literal: Advancing from Wenshui to suppress, he pacified the old nest at Luzhu Mountain, received the surrender of Tiejiangping, Jiucangba, and more than twenty cave strongholds of those who had been coerced.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing from Wenshui, he suppressed the old stronghold at Luzhu Mountain and accepted the surrender of Tiejiangping, Jiucangba, and more than twenty cave hideouts whose occupants had been forced into rebellion.

sentences.zh: 六年，破沙窩踞賊，解大定圍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he defeated bandits entrenched at Shawo and lifted the siege of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he broke the rebels holding Shawo and relieved the siege of Dading.

sentences.zh: 拔大屯朵壩賊壘，會滇軍平豬拱箐苗，又拔平遠牛場坉苗巢。

translations.literal: He captured the bandit fortifications at Datunduoba, joined Yunnan armies to pacify the Miao at Zhugongqing, and also captured the Miao nest at Pingyuan Niuchangtun.
translations.idiomatic: He overran the rebel fortifications at Datunduoba, joined Yunnan forces in pacifying the Miao at Zhugongqing, and also took the Miao stronghold at Pingyuan Niuchangtun.

sentences.zh: 黔西肅清。

translations.literal: Western Guizhou was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Western Guizhou was cleared of rebels.

sentences.zh: 七年，疏陳雲南軍事，命赴本任。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he memorialized reporting on military affairs in Yunnan and was ordered to proceed to his proper post.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he memorialized on the military situation in Yunnan and was ordered to take up his appointed post.

sentences.zh: 尋擢雲貴總督，駐軍曲靖。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou and encamped his army at Qujing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon elevated to Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou and stationed his army at Qujing.

sentences.zh: 進攻尋甸，破七星橋木城，扼文筆山、法鼓山要衝，剷平附近村莊賊壘。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Xundian, destroyed the wooden fort at Qixing Bridge, seized the strategic passes of Wenbi Mountain and Fagu Mountain, and leveled bandit fortifications in nearby villages.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against Xundian, destroyed the wooden fort at Qixing Bridge, secured the strategic heights of Wenbi Mountain and Fagu Mountain, and swept away rebel fortifications in the surrounding villages.

sentences.zh: 收復果馬，疊捷於塘子、張徐灣諸處。

translations.literal: He recovered Guoma and achieved repeated victories at Tangzi, Zhangxuwan, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Guoma and won a series of victories at Tangzi, Zhangxu Bay, and other points.

sentences.zh: 援賊大至，圍攻果馬，各營皆陷，革職留任。

translations.literal: Relieving bandits arrived in great force, besieged and attacked Guoma, all the camps fell, and he was dismissed from office but retained in his post.
translations.idiomatic: A large rebel relief force arrived, besieged Guoma, and overran every camp; he was stripped of rank but kept in command.

sentences.zh: 八年，解馬龍圍，進逼尋甸，賊首馬天順、李芳園乞撫，遂復其城。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he lifted the siege of Malong, advanced to press Xundian; the bandit chieftains Ma Tianshun and Li Fangyuan begged for pacification, and the city was then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he broke the siege of Malong and pressed on toward Xundian; the rebel leaders Ma Tianshun and Li Fangyuan sued for surrender, and the city was recovered.

sentences.zh: 雲南捻亂已久，各軍惟布政使岑毓英所部最強，而毓英素尚意氣，岳昭開誠專任，調發進止悉聽之。

translations.literal: The Nian rebellion in Yunnan had long continued; among the various armies only the forces of Provincial Administration Commissioner Cen Yuying were strongest; yet Yuying had always prized personal honor; Yuezhao opened his heart and entrusted him fully; dispatch, advance, and halt were entirely at his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan had long been torn by rebellion, and among the various armies Cen Yuying's force—the provincial administration commissioner—was the strongest; as Cen was a man of strong personal pride, Liu Yuezhao put his full trust in him and left all decisions on deployment and maneuver entirely to his judgment.

sentences.zh: 毓英尋擢巡撫，和衷無牽制，軍事日有起色。

translations.literal: Yuying was soon promoted to Governor; in harmony without restraint, military affairs daily improved.
translations.idiomatic: When Cen Yuying was soon promoted to governor, the two worked in harmony without interference, and the military situation steadily improved.

sentences.zh: 九年，克麗江，复威遠、姚州，复永北、鶴慶、鎮南、鄧川、浪穹，拔鳳羽白米莊賊巢，平彌勒縣竹園踞匪。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he captured Lijiang, recovered Weiyuan and Yaozhou, recovered Yongbei, Heqing, Zhennan, Dengchuan, and Langqiong, captured the bandit nest at Fengyu Baimizhuang, and pacified bandits entrenched at Zhuyuan in Mile County.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he took Lijiang, recovered Weiyuan and Yaozhou, Yongbei, Heqing, Zhennan, Dengchuan, and Langqiong, overran the rebel stronghold at Fengyu Baimizhuang, and pacified the rebels holding Zhuyuan in Mile County.

sentences.zh: 十年，平永善蠻匪，拔賓州賊巢，平香爐山槓匪，連克河西之大東溝、小東溝及臨安之五山夷寨。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he pacified barbarian bandits in Yongshan, captured the bandit nest in Binzhou, pacified gang bandits on Xianglu Mountain, and in succession captured Dadonggou and Xiaodonggou in Hexi and the five mountain Yi stockades in Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he pacified the tribal rebels in Yongshan, stormed the rebel nest in Binzhou, cleared the brigand gangs on Xianglu Mountain, and in succession took Dadonggou and Xiaodonggou west of the river and the five Yi stockades in the Lin'an hills.

sentences.zh: 十一年，复貴州興義新城，先後克永平、雲南及趙州、蒙化廳各城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he recovered Xingyi New City in Guizhou and in succession captured the cities of Yongping, Yunnan, Zhaozhou, and Menghua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he recovered Xingyi New City in Guizhou and went on to capture Yongping, Yunnan, Zhaozhou, and Menghua Prefecture in turn.

sentences.zh: 攻大理上下兩關，復大理府城，誅大酋杜文秀，詔復原職。

translations.literal: He attacked the upper and lower passes of Dali, recovered Dali Prefectural City, executed the great chieftain Du Wenxiu, and an edict restored his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: He assaulted the upper and lower passes of Dali, recovered the prefectural city, executed the rebel leader Du Wenxiu, and an edict restored Liu Yuezhao to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 十二年，滇省肅清，賜黃馬褂，疏請陛見。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Yunnan Province was cleared; he was granted a yellow riding jacket and memorialized requesting an audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Yunnan was fully pacified; he was granted a yellow riding jacket and memorialized requesting an audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，以入覲遷延，御史李廷簫劾其規避，下部議褫職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, because his presentation at court was delayed, Censor Li Tingshao impeached him for evasion; the matter was referred to the ministry for deliberation and dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu, because he had long delayed coming to court for an audience, Censor Li Tingshao impeached him for deliberate evasion; the case was referred to the ministry for deliberation, and he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died.

sentences.zh: 署湖南巡撫龐際雲疏陳：「岳昭統兵十餘年，建功之地，黔屬為多；

translations.literal: Acting Hunan Governor Pang Jiyun memorialized: "Yuezhao commanded troops for more than ten years; the place where he achieved the most merit was mostly Guizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Acting Hunan Governor Pang Jiyun memorialized: "Liu Yuezhao commanded troops for more than ten years; most of his achievements were won in Guizhou;

sentences.zh: 任事之艱，雲南為最；

translations.literal: the hardship of his service was greatest in Yunnan;
translations.idiomatic: the greatest hardships of his service were borne in Yunnan;

sentences.zh: 請復原官。」

translations.literal: I request that his original rank be restored."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that his original rank be restored."

sentences.zh: 詔允之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict granted the request.

sentences.zh: 岳昭之規尋甸也，杜文秀遣黨萬餘，戰不利。

translations.literal: When Yuezhao was threatening Xundian, Du Wenxiu sent more than ten thousand followers; the battle went unfavorably.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuezhao was moving against Xundian, Du Wenxiu sent more than ten thousand men against him, and the battle went badly.

sentences.zh: 從弟岳晙請岳昭速還曲靖，以固根本。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Yue Jun asked Yuezhao to hurry back to Qujing to secure the base.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Liu Yuejun urged Liu Yuezhao to return quickly to Qujing and secure their base.

sentences.zh: 賊果分黨往襲，以有備不得逞。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed sent a separate detachment to attack; because preparations had been made, they could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did in fact send a separate force to strike at Qujing, but finding the defenses ready, they could not carry out their plan.

sentences.zh: 岳晙守馬龍，賊圍之，伺懈出擊，走之。

translations.literal: Yue Jun defended Malong; the bandits besieged it; he watched for slackness and sallied forth to attack, driving them off.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuejun held Malong; when rebels besieged the city, he waited for a lapse in their vigilance, sallied out to attack, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 固守數月，練兵得三千人，會攻尋甸，破七星橋要隘，賊蹙乞降，猶懷反側，岳晙率三十人入城，示以坦白，人心始定。

translations.literal: He held fast for several months, drilled his troops to three thousand men, then joined the attack on Xundian, broke the strategic pass at Qixing Bridge, pressed the bandits until they begged to surrender though still wavering in loyalty; Yue Jun led thirty men into the city, showed them open sincerity, and hearts were finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: He held his position for months, trained his force to three thousand men, then joined the assault on Xundian and broke the strategic pass at Qixing Bridge; when the rebels, cornered, sued for surrender but still seemed unreliable, Liu Yuejun entered the city with thirty men, showed them complete candor, and the townspeople at last settled down.

sentences.zh: 次日，毓英兵亦至，服其膽略。

translations.literal: The next day Yuying's troops also arrived, and he admired his boldness and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Cen Yuying's force arrived as well, and he was impressed by Liu Yuejun's boldness and skill.

sentences.zh: 岳晙先以積功擢至道員，岳昭至滇後，專任毓英滇軍，其舊部多遣去雲。

translations.literal: Yue Jun had earlier been promoted through accumulated merit to the rank of Circuit Intendant; after Yuezhao reached Yunnan, he entrusted the Yunnan army solely to Yuying, and sent most of his old subordinates back to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuejun had already risen through accumulated merit to the rank of circuit intendant; after Liu Yuezhao reached Yunnan, he put the provincial army entirely under Cen Yuying and sent most of his old officers back to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 岑毓英，字彥卿，廣西西林人。

translations.literal: Cen Yuying, courtesy name Yanqing, was a native of Xilin in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Yuying, styled Yanqing, was a native of Xilin in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He held the degree of licentiate.

sentences.zh: 治鄉團，擊土匪，以功敘縣丞。

translations.literal: He organized local militia, struck at bandits, and through merit was appointed Acting Assistant Magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He organized local militia, fought bandits, and for his service was appointed acting assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，率勇赴雲南迤西助剿回匪。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Xianfeng reign, he led braves to western Yunnan to assist in suppressing Hui bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Xianfeng reign, he led militia to western Yunnan to help suppress the Hui rebels.

sentences.zh: 九年，克宜良，權縣事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he captured Yiliang and acted as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he took Yiliang and served as acting county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 十年，克路南，署州事，擢同知直隸州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he captured Ludian, acted as prefect, and was promoted to Sub-Prefect of Zhili Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he captured Ludian, served as acting prefect, and was promoted to sub-prefect of Zhili Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 進攻澂江，兼署知府。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Chengjiang and also served as acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against Chengjiang and concurrently served as acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 十一年，克澂江賊壘，破昆陽海口賊，迤西回匪連陷楚雄、廣通、祿豐，省城戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he captured the bandit fortifications at Chengjiang, defeated the bandits at Kunyang Haikou; Hui bandits in western Yunnan in succession captured Chuxiong, Guangtong, and Lufeng, and the provincial capital was placed under martial alert.
