translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he stormed the rebel fortifications at Chengjiang and defeated the rebels at Kunyang Haikou; meanwhile Hui rebels in western Yunnan overran Chuxiong, Guangtong, and Lufeng in succession, and the provincial capital was placed on high alert.

sentences.zh: 毓英赴援，同治元年，破賊大樹營。

translations.literal: Yuying went to the relief; in the first year of the Tongzhi reign he defeated the bandits at Dashuying.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Yuying marched to the relief, and in the first year of the Tongzhi reign he routed the rebels at Dashuying.

sentences.zh: 時總督張亮基引疾去，巡撫徐之銘主撫，回酋馬如龍通款，毓英往諭順逆，如龍獻所踞新興等八城，之銘奏以毓英攝布政使。

translations.literal: At that time Governor-General Zhang Liangji retired on grounds of illness; Governor Xu Zhiming favored pacification; the Hui chieftain Ma Rulong opened communications; Yuying went to instruct him on loyalty and rebellion; Rulong surrendered the eight cities he held, including Xinxing; Zhiming memorialized appointing Yuying Acting Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Governor-General Zhang Liangji withdrew on grounds of illness; Governor Xu Zhiming favored a policy of pacification; the Hui chieftain Ma Rulong entered negotiations; Cen Yuying went to explain the difference between loyalty and rebellion; Ma Rulong surrendered the eight cities he held, including Xinxing; Xu Zhiming memorialized for Cen Yuying to serve as acting provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋以安撫功，加按察使銜，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Soon, for his pacification achievements, he was given the rank of Surveillance Commissioner and granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for his work in pacification, he was given the rank of surveillance commissioner and awarded a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 二年，回弁馬榮叛，戕總督潘鐸，毓英率所部粵勇一千，與弟毓寶等守籓署。

translations.literal: In the second year the Hui officer Ma Rong rebelled and assassinated Governor-General Pan Duo; Yuying led a thousand Cantonese braves under his command, and with his younger brother Yu Bao and others defended the provincial administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the Hui officer Ma Rong rebelled and murdered Governor-General Pan Duo; Cen Yuying led a thousand Cantonese militiamen under his command, and with his younger brother Yu Bao and others held the provincial administration compound.

sentences.zh: 之銘微服詣毓英，司道皆集，分兵守東、南門，密召馬如龍入援。

translations.literal: Zhiming went in plain dress to seek out Yuying; all the provincial and circuit officials gathered; troops were divided to guard the eastern and southern gates; Ma Rulong was secretly summoned to enter and reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhiming went in disguise to consult Cen Yuying; the provincial and circuit officials all assembled; troops were posted at the eastern and southern gates; and Ma Rulong was secretly summoned to come to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 如龍至，誅亂黨，馬榮跳走南寧，合馬聯昇踞曲靖八屬。

translations.literal: When Rulong arrived, the disorderly faction was executed; Ma Rong fled to Nanning and joined Ma Liansheng in holding the eight districts of Qujing.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Rulong arrived, the mutineers were put to death; Ma Rong fled to Nanning and joined Ma Liansheng in holding the eight districts of Qujing.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉毓英守城功，擢道員。

translations.literal: An edict praised Yuying's merit in defending the city, and he was promoted to Circuit Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended Cen Yuying for defending the city, and he was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 率師西剿，复富民、安寧、羅次、高明、祿豐、武定、祿勸、廣通、陸涼、南安諸城，及黑、元、永三鹽井，進搗楚雄。

translations.literal: He led his army west in suppression, recovered Fumin, Anning, Luoci, Gaoming, Lufeng, Wuding, Luquan, Guangtong, Liuliang, and Nan'an and other cities, together with the three salt wells of Hei, Yuan, and Yong, and advanced to strike at Chuxiong.
translations.idiomatic: He led his army west in suppression, recovered Fumin, Anning, Luoci, Gaoming, Lufeng, Wuding, Luquan, Guangtong, Liuliang, Nan'an, and other cities, together with the three salt wells of Hei, Yuan, and Yong, and advanced to strike at Chuxiong.

sentences.zh: 會東路有警，之銘檄回省，分兵克霑益、平彝。

translations.literal: When an alarm arose on the eastern route, Zhiming ordered him back to the provincial capital; detachments were sent to capture Zhanyi and Pingyi.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble broke out on the eastern front, Xu Zhiming ordered him back to the provincial capital and sent detachments to capture Zhanyi and Pingyi.

sentences.zh: 赴楚雄督攻，克其城。

translations.literal: He went to Chuxiong to supervise the assault and captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Chuxiong to direct the assault and took the city.

sentences.zh: 進復大姚、雲南、趙州、賓川、鄧川、浪穹、鶴慶，分道進規大理上下關。

translations.literal: He advanced to recover Dayao, Yunnan, Zhaozhou, Binchuan, Dengchuan, Langqiong, and Heqing, and sent separate columns to move against the upper and lower passes of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to recover Dayao, Yunnan, Zhaozhou, Binchuan, Dengchuan, Langqiong, and Heqing, and sent separate columns to move against the upper and lower passes of Dali.

sentences.zh: 三年，克定遠，圍攻鎮南，大破援賊於普棚。

translations.literal: In the third year he captured Dingyuan, besieged and attacked Zhennan, and inflicted a great defeat on relieving bandits at Pupeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he captured Dingyuan, besieged Zhennan, and routed a large rebel relief force at Pupeng.

sentences.zh: 馬聯昇复陷霑益，犯馬龍，回軍破之於天生關。

translations.literal: Ma Liansheng again captured Zhanyi and invaded Malong; Yuying turned his army back and defeated him at Tiansheng Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Liansheng again captured Zhanyi and invaded Malong; Cen Yuying wheeled his army about and defeated him at Tiansheng Pass.

sentences.zh: 進攻曲靖，复馬龍、霑益。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Qujing and recovered Malong and Zhanyi.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against Qujing and recovered Malong and Zhanyi.

sentences.zh: 進克尋甸，擒馬榮、馬興才，克曲靖，擒馬聯昇，並誅之。

translations.literal: He then captured Xundian, seized Ma Rong and Ma Xingcai, captured Qujing, seized Ma Liansheng, and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Xundian, captured Ma Rong and Ma Xingcai, took Qujing, captured Ma Liansheng, and had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 尚書趙光疏呈滇紳公啟，言毓英所向有功，特詔嘉勉，下總督勞崇光據實保奏。

translations.literal: Minister Zhao Guang submitted a memorial presenting a joint petition from Yunnan gentry, stating that wherever Yuying advanced he achieved merit; a special edict commended and encouraged him, and orders were sent to Governor-General Lao Chongguang to recommend him according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhao Guang submitted a memorial with a joint petition from Yunnan gentry stating that Cen Yuying had won success wherever he fought; a special edict commended him, and Governor-General Lao Chongguang was instructed to recommend him on merit.

sentences.zh: 四年，肅清迤東，加布政使銜，賜號勉勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the eastern route was cleared; he was given the rank of Provincial Administration Commissioner and granted the title Brave and Resolute Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the eastern region was cleared; he was given the rank of provincial administration commissioner and granted the title Brave and Resolute Batulu.

sentences.zh: 西路自毓英軍移去，所克諸城多復陷，僅存楚雄未失。

translations.literal: After Yuying's army withdrew from the western route, most of the cities he had captured were lost again; only Chuxiong remained untaken.
translations.idiomatic: After Cen Yuying's army withdrew from the western front, most of the cities he had recovered were lost again; only Chuxiong still held.

sentences.zh: 毓英駐軍曲靖，護省城運道。

translations.literal: Yuying stationed his army at Qujing and protected the supply route to the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Yuying encamped at Qujing and guarded the supply route to the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 五年，命署布政使，勞崇光至是始至滇受事，奏以提督馬如龍專辦西路，令毓英督剿豬拱箐苗。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was ordered to serve as Acting Provincial Administration Commissioner; Lao Chongguang only then arrived in Yunnan to take up his duties; he memorialized that Ma Rulong as Military Governor should be entrusted exclusively with the western route, and that Yuying should supervise the suppression of the Miao at Zhugongqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed acting provincial administration commissioner; Lao Chongguang had only just arrived in Yunnan to take office; he memorialized that Military Governor Ma Rulong should be put in sole charge of the western front and that Cen Yuying should supervise the campaign against the Miao at Zhugongqing.

sentences.zh: 豬拱箐隸貴州威寧州，與海馬姑相犄角，山溪阻深，苗酋陶新春、陶三春分據之。

translations.literal: Zhugongqing was under Weining Prefecture in Guizhou; it stood in mutual support with Haimagu; mountains and streams were steep and deep; the Miao chieftains Tao Xinchun and Tao San Chun held it between them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhugongqing fell under Weining Prefecture in Guizhou; it stood in mutual support with Haimagu; the mountains and streams were steep and treacherous; and the Miao chieftains Tao Xinchun and Tao San Chun held it between them.

sentences.zh: 糾聚苗、教諸匪及粵匪石達開餘黨，凡十數万人，迭擾滇之鎮雄、彝良、大關、昭通，黔之大定、黔西、威寧、畢節，且及川疆，三省會剿久無功。

translations.literal: They gathered Miao bandits, sectarian bandits, and the remnants of Shi Dakai's Cantonese rebels, altogether more than one hundred thousand men, and repeatedly raided Zhenxiong, Yiliang, Daguan, and Zhaotong in Yunnan, Dading, Qianxi, Weining, and Bijie in Guizhou, and even reached the Sichuan frontier; joint suppression by the three provinces long achieved no success.
translations.idiomatic: They gathered Miao rebels, sectarian rebels, and the remnants of Shi Dakai's Cantonese forces, more than one hundred thousand men in all, and repeatedly raided Zhenxiong, Yiliang, Daguan, and Zhaotong in Yunnan, Dading, Qianxi, Weining, and Bijie in Guizhou, and even reached into Sichuan; joint campaigns by all three provinces had long failed to gain success.

sentences.zh: 毓英上書駱秉章，謂權不一則軍不用命，原率滇軍獨任，期百二十日覆其巢，授迤西道，署布政使如故。

translations.literal: Yuying wrote to Luo Bingzhang, stating that where authority was not unified the army would not obey orders; he volunteered to lead the Yunnan army alone, pledging to destroy their nest within one hundred twenty days; he was appointed Circuit Intendant for Western Yunnan and continued to serve as Acting Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Yuying wrote to Luo Bingzhang saying that divided authority meant troops would not obey; he offered to lead the Yunnan army alone and pledged to destroy the rebel base within one hundred twenty days; he was appointed circuit intendant for western Yunnan while continuing as acting provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二月，師抵豬拱箐，令張保和、林守懷領二千人，由大溜口出二龍關後，掩襲吳家屯，自督三千人攻關。

translations.literal: In the second month the army reached Zhugongqing; he ordered Zhang Baohe and Lin Shouhuai to lead two thousand men through Daliekou to emerge behind Erlong Pass and make a surprise attack on Wujiatun, while he personally directed three thousand men in assaulting the pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the army reached Zhugongqing; he ordered Zhang Baohe and Lin Shouhuai to lead two thousand men through Daliekou to emerge behind Erlong Pass and surprise Wujiatun, while he personally directed three thousand men in the assault on the pass.

sentences.zh: 賊傾巢出戰，關後砲發，賊回救，毓英揮軍夾擊，三隘皆下，遂奪吳家屯，擒斬數千。

translations.literal: The bandits came out in full force to fight; cannon fired from behind the pass; the bandits turned back to the rescue; Yuying directed his army in a pincer attack; all three passes were taken; Wujiatun was then captured and several thousand were seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came out in full force; cannon opened fire from behind the pass; the rebels wheeled back to save it; Cen Yuying launched a pincer attack; all three passes fell; Wujiatun was then captured and several thousand rebels were killed or taken.

sentences.zh: 賊自海馬姑來援，截擊之，斬其酋，餘賊反奔。

translations.literal: Bandits came from Haimagu to reinforce; he intercepted and attacked them, beheaded their chieftain, and the remaining bandits fled back in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel reinforcements came from Haimagu; he intercepted and attacked them, beheaded their chieftain, and the rest fled in retreat.

sentences.zh: 令蔡標、劉重慶分軍圍剿海馬姑，克紅岩、尖山，賊援乃斷，遂逼豬拱箐老巢。

translations.literal: He ordered Cai Biao and Liu Chongqing to divide their forces and besiege Haimagu; they captured Hongyan and Jianshan; rebel reinforcements were then cut off, and he pressed on toward the main nest at Zhugongqing.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Cai Biao and Liu Chongqing to divide their forces and besiege Haimagu; they captured Hongyan and Jianshan; rebel reinforcements were cut off, and he pressed on toward the main stronghold at Zhugongqing.

sentences.zh: 賊以巨石自山顛墜下，驅牛馬突營，將士多傷亡，毓英督軍搏戰，斬悍酋，賊始卻。

translations.literal: The bandits rolled down huge stones from the mountain crest and drove cattle and horses in a charge against the camp; many officers and soldiers were killed or wounded; Yuying directed the army in close combat, beheaded a fierce chieftain, and the bandits at last withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels rolled huge stones down from the mountain crest and drove cattle and horses in a charge against the camp; many officers and men were killed or wounded; Cen Yuying led the army in close combat, killed a fierce chieftain, and the rebels at last fell back.

sentences.zh: 於營前掘深坎，賊所發石盡陷坎內，誘降倮人，得賊虛實，選敢死士二千，填壕以進，連破木城二，直搗其巢，縱火焚之，斬馘二萬，擒陶新春及其死黨，磔之，拔山男婦四萬餘人。

translations.literal: He dug deep trenches before the camp so that all the stones the bandits launched fell into them; he induced the Luo people to surrender and learned the bandits' true strength; he selected two thousand dare-to-die men to fill the moats and advance, broke through two wooden forts in succession, struck straight at their nest, set fire and burned it, killed and beheaded twenty thousand, captured Tao Xinchun and his diehard followers and dismembered them, and rescued more than forty thousand men and women from the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He dug deep trenches before the camp so that the stones the rebels hurled all fell into them; he induced the Luo people to surrender and learned the rebels' dispositions; he picked two thousand volunteers to fill the ditches and press forward, broke through two wooden forts in succession, struck straight at the stronghold, burned it, killed or captured twenty thousand rebels, seized Tao Xinchun and his diehard followers and had them dismembered, and rescued more than forty thousand men and women from the mountains.

sentences.zh: 乘勝合攻海馬姑，伏兵山前後，進毀賊壘三十餘，以噴筒環燒，擒陶三春及悍酋二百餘人，皆斬之，賊悉平。

translations.literal: Pressing his advantage, he joined in the attack on Haimagu, set ambushes before and behind the mountains, advanced and destroyed more than thirty bandit fortifications, burned them round about with flame-projectors, captured Tao San Chun and more than two hundred fierce chieftains, all of whom were executed, and the bandits were completely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing his advantage, he combined forces to attack Haimagu, laid ambushes before and behind the hills, advanced and destroyed more than thirty rebel fortifications, burned them with flame-projectors on every side, captured Tao San Chun and more than two hundred fierce chieftains, had them all executed, and the rebels were completely pacified.

sentences.zh: 計自進兵至是，僅逾期四日，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: Counting from the opening of the campaign to this point, he was only four days past the deadline; he was granted a first-rank court hat button.
translations.idiomatic: From the opening of the campaign to this point, he was only four days past his deadline; he was granted a first-rank court hat button.

sentences.zh: 馬如龍剿迤西屢失利，勞崇光病歿，杜文秀大舉東犯，連陷二十餘城，省垣告急。

translations.literal: Ma Rulong's suppression campaigns in western Yunnan repeatedly met with setbacks; Lao Chongguang died of illness; Du Wenxiu launched a great eastern offensive, capturing more than twenty cities in succession; the provincial capital was in urgent danger.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rulong's campaigns in western Yunnan repeatedly ended in defeat; Lao Chongguang died of illness; Du Wenxiu launched a major eastern offensive and overran more than twenty cities in succession; the provincial capital was in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，毓英自豬拱箐凱旋曲靖，先遣弟毓寶助省防。

translations.literal: That winter Yuying returned in triumph from Zhugongqing to Qujing and first sent his younger brother Yu Bao to help defend the province.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Cen Yuying returned in triumph from Zhugongqing to Qujing and first sent his younger brother Yu Bao to help defend the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 七年春，揚言師出陸涼，而取道宜涼、七甸，連破大小石壩、小板橋、古庭庵、金馬寺賊壘，進屯大樹營。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year he publicly announced that his army would march out through Liuliang, but actually took the route through Yiliang and Qidian, successively breaking the bandit fortifications at large and small Shiba, Xiaobanqiao, Guting'an, and Jinmasi, and encamped at Dashuying.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he announced publicly that his army would march out through Liuliang, but actually took the route through Yiliang and Qidian, successively storming the rebel fortifications at large and small Shiba, Xiaobanqiao, Guting'an, and Jinmasi, and encamped at Dashuying.

sentences.zh: 馬如龍來會，人心始定。

translations.literal: When Ma Rulong came to join him, hearts were finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Rulong came to join him, morale at last steadied.

sentences.zh: 昆陽匪首楊震鵬夜渡昆明池襲省城，毓寶擊敗之，震鵬負創遁。

translations.literal: Yang Zhenpeng, bandit chieftain of Kunyang, crossed Kunming Lake by night to raid the provincial capital; Yu Bao defeated him, and Zhenpeng fled wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhenpeng, the rebel leader of Kunyang, crossed Kunming Lake by night to strike at the provincial capital; Yu Bao defeated him, and Yang fled wounded.

sentences.zh: 進攻楊林，毓英鼻受槍傷，回軍省城，連破石虎關賊壘，擒賊渠李洪勳，擢授巡撫。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Yanglin; Yuying was wounded in the nose by gunfire; he returned his army to the provincial capital, successively broke the bandit fortifications at Shihuguan, captured the bandit leader Li Hongxun, and was promoted and appointed Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against Yanglin; Cen Yuying was wounded in the nose by gunfire; he withdrew to the provincial capital, successively stormed the rebel fortifications at Shihuguan, captured the rebel leader Li Hongxun, and was promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 附省賊壘猶繁，與之相持。

translations.literal: Bandit fortifications near the provincial capital were still numerous, and he remained locked in stalemate with them.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel fortifications near the provincial capital were still numerous, and he remained locked in stalemate with them.

sentences.zh: 總督劉岳昭初至滇，由馬龍進剿尋甸​​，失利，賊勢复熾。

translations.literal: When Governor-General Liu Yuezhao first reached Yunnan, he advanced from Malong to suppress Xundian, met with defeat, and the bandit power revived.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor-General Liu Yuezhao first reached Yunnan, he advanced from Malong to suppress Xundian, suffered a defeat, and rebel strength revived.

sentences.zh: 毓英疏陳軍事、餉事，略曰：「杜文秀竊踞迤西十有三載，根深蒂固。

translations.literal: Yuying memorialized on military and supply affairs, briefly stating: "Du Wenxiu has usurped control of western Yunnan for thirteen years; his roots run deep and his foundation is firm.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Yuying submitted a detailed memorial on military and fiscal affairs, opening with: "Du Wenxiu has held western Yunnan for thirteen years; his power is deeply entrenched.

sentences.zh: 今擬三路進兵，一出迤南牽賊勢，一出三姚、永北斷賊援，大軍由楚雄、鎮南直搗中堅，使賊面面受敵，不能兼顧。

translations.literal: It is now proposed to advance with three routes: one out of southern Yunnan to pin down the bandits' strength, one out of Sanyao and Yongbei to cut off bandit reinforcements, and the main army through Chuxiong and Zhennan to strike straight at the central stronghold, so that the bandits will be attacked on every side and unable to attend to all fronts.
translations.idiomatic: I now propose a three-pronged advance: one column out of southern Yunnan to tie down the rebels, one out of Sanyao and Yongbei to sever their reinforcements, and the main force through Chuxiong and Zhennan to strike at their core, so that the enemy will be attacked on every side and unable to cover all fronts.

sentences.zh: 臣選精銳六萬，更番戰守，既無停兵之時，亦免師老之患。

translations.literal: Your subject selects sixty thousand elite troops to rotate in combat and defense; there will be no pause in fighting, and the danger of an army growing stale will also be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: I propose to field sixty thousand picked troops in rotating combat and garrison duty, so that fighting never stops and the army never grows stale.

sentences.zh: 兵勇無須外募，以本省兵剿本省賊，既習地利，复熟賊情。

translations.literal: Soldiers and braves need not be recruited from outside; using the province's own troops to suppress the province's own bandits, they are familiar with the terrain and also know the bandits' dispositions.
translations.idiomatic: There is no need to recruit from outside the province; troops fighting their own province's rebels know the terrain and understand the enemy.

sentences.zh: 現在滇省兵勇鄉團已調集八萬有奇，擬俟附省逆壘肅清，認真裁汰，選定精銳，以資得力。

translations.literal: At present more than eighty thousand soldiers, braves, and local militia have been assembled in Yunnan Province; after the rebel fortifications near the provincial capital are cleared, rigorous reductions are planned, and chosen elites will be selected to make the force effective.
translations.idiomatic: More than eighty thousand regular troops, militia, and local levies have now been assembled in Yunnan; once the rebel strongholds near the capital are cleared, I propose a rigorous cutback and the selection of an elite force that can actually fight.

sentences.zh: 滇省綠營額設馬步兵三萬七千數百名，承平日久，訓練多疏，將不知兵，兵不知戰。

translations.literal: Yunnan Province's Green Standard Army is allotted more than thirty-seven thousand cavalry and infantry; after long years of peace training has mostly been neglected; officers do not know warfare, and soldiers do not know how to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's Green Standard Army is allotted more than thirty-seven thousand cavalry and infantry; after long years of peace, training has mostly lapsed; officers no longer know war, and soldiers no longer know how to fight.

sentences.zh: 倉卒有事，則募勇以代兵；

translations.literal: When trouble arises suddenly, braves are recruited to replace regular troops;
translations.idiomatic: When trouble breaks out suddenly, militia are recruited to replace regular troops;

sentences.zh: 餉需支絀，不能不後兵而先勇。

translations.literal: because pay cannot keep up with needs, braves must come before regular troops in allotment.
translations.idiomatic: because funds cannot keep pace with demand, militia pay must come before regular army pay.

sentences.zh: 於是兵丁愈困，營務益弛。

translations.literal: Thus the regular soldiers grow ever more destitute and camp discipline grows ever laxer.
translations.idiomatic: Regular soldiers grow poorer and camp discipline grows laxer.

sentences.zh: 通省營兵所存不及十一，臣擬即此六萬人中，擇補營額，目前仍令隨徵，事竣再飭歸伍。

translations.literal: Of the provincial garrison less than one part in ten remains; your subject proposes to select replacements for garrison quotas from these sixty thousand men, and for the present still to have them follow the campaign, restoring them to their posts only when the affair is concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Less than one tenth of the provincial garrison still survives; I propose to fill garrison quotas from these sixty thousand men, keep them on campaign for now, and only return them to their posts when the war is over.

sentences.zh: 既有常業，自有恆心，責以成功，收效必速。

translations.literal: Once they have steady employment they will have steady resolve; charged with success, results will surely come quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Men with steady employment will have steady resolve; given clear expectations of success, results will come quickly.

sentences.zh: 滇省近年用兵，多藉鄉勇之力，擬按州縣之大小，定徵調之多寡，共編鄉勇四十營，分兩班隨營征討，餉銀仍由各地籌捐。

translations.literal: In recent years Yunnan has relied heavily on local militia in warfare; it is proposed to set quotas for mobilization according to the size of each prefecture and county, altogether organizing forty battalions of local militia, divided into two shifts to follow the camps in campaign, with pay still raised by local contributions.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years Yunnan has relied heavily on local militia; I propose to set mobilization quotas by prefecture and county size, organize forty battalions of local militia in two rotating shifts to campaign with the regular forces, and continue to raise their pay through local contributions.

sentences.zh: 兩年之內，迤西肅清，即可裁撤歸農。

translations.literal: Within two years, once western Yunnan is cleared, they can be disbanded and sent back to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years, once western Yunnan is pacified, they can be disbanded and sent back to the fields.

sentences.zh: 滇省兵勇，向於餉銀之外，每名月支米三斗。

translations.literal: Soldiers and braves in Yunnan Province, in addition to cash pay, have each received three dou of rice per month.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's soldiers and militia have customarily received three dou of rice per man each month in addition to their silver pay.

sentences.zh: 現擬用兵六萬，每年共需米二十餘萬石，為數甚鉅。

translations.literal: It is now proposed to employ sixty thousand troops, requiring more than two hundred thousand shi of rice each year—a very large figure.
translations.idiomatic: A force of sixty thousand would require more than two hundred thousand shi of rice each year—a very large figure.

sentences.zh: 歷年皆按成熟田畝酌抽釐穀，約十分取其一二，資助軍食，與川之津貼，黔之義穀，名異實同。

translations.literal: Over the years grain has been assessed by the acre on ripened fields, about one or two parts in ten, to support army rations; this differs in name from Sichuan's subsidies and Guizhou's righteous grain, but is the same in substance.
translations.idiomatic: For years grain has been levied on ripe fields at about one or two parts in ten to feed the army; it differs in name from Sichuan's subsidies and Guizhou's righteous grain, but amounts to the same thing.

sentences.zh: 今請照舊抽收，並將近年可徵地丁抽糧，全數改徵糧米，如不敷用，再行籌價採買接濟，一俟軍事肅清，分別裁止。

translations.literal: It is now requested that collection continue as before, and that recent land-tax grain that can be collected be converted entirely into grain levies; if this is still insufficient, prices may be raised to purchase supplies; once military affairs are settled, these measures will be ended separately.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this levy continue as before, and that recent land-tax grain collections be converted entirely into grain rations; if that still falls short, funds can be raised to buy grain; once the war is over, these measures can be ended.

sentences.zh: 滇省綠營官兵俸餉，有閏之年，需銀七十萬兩有奇，無閏需銀六十四萬數千兩。

translations.literal: Salaries and pay for Green Standard officers and soldiers in Yunnan Province, in years with an intercalary month, require more than seven hundred thousand taels of silver; in years without, more than six hundred forty thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Salaries and pay for Yunnan's Green Standard officers and soldiers require more than seven hundred thousand taels of silver in intercalary years and more than six hundred forty thousand in ordinary years.

sentences.zh: 現既易勇為兵，則餉銀較勇糧稍厚。

translations.literal: Since braves are now being converted into regular troops, silver pay will be somewhat more generous than brave rations.
translations.idiomatic: Since militia are now being converted into regular troops, silver pay will be somewhat higher than militia rations.

sentences.zh: 倘因籌餉維艱，每月先給半餉，加以賞需軍火各費，約共需銀八萬兩。

translations.literal: If raising funds proves difficult, half pay may first be issued each month, together with rewards, ammunition, and other expenses—altogether about eighty thousand taels required.
translations.idiomatic: If funds are hard to raise, half pay may be issued each month, together with rewards, ammunition, and other costs—about eighty thousand taels in all.

sentences.zh: 鹽課、地丁、釐稅之外，每月所短不過三四萬兩，應由外省協撥，較之向例協餉，有減無增。

translations.literal: Beyond salt tax, land tax, and transit dues, the monthly shortfall would be no more than thirty or forty thousand taels, which should be supplied by other provinces—less than the customary co-supplied pay and not more.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond salt tax, land tax, and transit dues, the monthly shortfall would be no more than thirty or forty thousand taels, which other provinces should supply—less than the usual co-supplied pay.

sentences.zh: 若發全餉，則每月應由外省撥銀六萬，較常例所增亦屬無幾。

translations.literal: If full pay is issued, then each month other provinces should allocate sixty thousand taels of silver—an increase over the usual amount, but not by much.
translations.idiomatic: If full pay is issued, other provinces would need to send sixty thousand taels a month—somewhat more than usual, but not greatly so.

sentences.zh: 現在部臣指撥各省協滇軍餉，如浙江、廣東、江西，距滇較遠，籌撥起解，往返經年，緩難濟急。

translations.literal: At present the ministry has assigned co-supplied Yunnan army pay from provinces such as Zhejiang, Guangdong, and Jiangxi; these are far from Yunnan, and raising and dispatching funds takes a full year round trip—too slow to meet urgent need.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry has currently assigned co-supplied army pay from provinces such as Zhejiang, Guangdong, and Jiangxi; these are far from Yunnan, and raising and dispatching funds takes a full year—too slow for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 請飭改作京餉，另由川、楚等省應解京餉，改撥濟滇，兩無窒礙。

translations.literal: It is requested that this be changed to capital stipends, with Sichuan, Huguang, and other provinces instead redirecting capital stipends due to aid Yunnan, so that neither arrangement is obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this be converted to capital stipends, with Sichuan, Huguang, and other provinces redirecting capital stipends to Yunnan instead, so that neither system is blocked.

sentences.zh: 至於選任鎮將，宜不拘資格，不惜情面，凡有能將三千兵以上，才當一面者，雖其名位尚卑，亦宜委署要職。

translations.literal: As for selecting military governors and generals, qualifications should not be rigidly observed and favoritism should not be spared; anyone capable of commanding more than three thousand troops and talent fit to hold one front, even if his name and rank are still low, should be entrusted with an important acting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In appointing military governors and generals, rank should not be rigidly observed nor favoritism spared; any man capable of commanding more than three thousand troops and fit to hold a front—even if his rank is still low—should be given an important acting post.

sentences.zh: 其謀勇平常，僅止熟習營務，縱系實缺，另予差遣，勿使幸位。」

translations.literal: Those whose plans and courage are ordinary and who only know camp routine well, even if they hold substantive appointments, should be given other assignments and not allowed to keep their posts through luck."
translations.idiomatic: Men whose plans and courage are ordinary and who merely know camp routine, even if they hold substantive posts, should be given other assignments and not allowed to keep their positions by luck."

sentences.zh: 疏入，下部如所議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the ministry approved and acted as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, and the ministry approved its recommendations.

sentences.zh: 八年春，賊酋楊榮率眾數万踞楊林長坡，分黨踞小偏橋、十里鋪、羊芳凹、牛街、興福寺，省城大震。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year the bandit chieftain Yang Rong led a force of tens of thousands holding Changpo at Yanglin; separate factions held Xiaopianqiao, Shilipu, Yangfang'ao, Niujie, and Xingfusi; the provincial capital was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year the rebel chieftain Yang Rong led tens of thousands of men holding Changpo at Yanglin; separate bands held Xiaopianqiao, Shilipu, Yangfang'ao, Niujie, and Xingfusi; the provincial capital was greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 毓英督諸軍分剿，奪回小偏橋諸處，复連敗之於蕭家山、鸚鵡山，擒斬逾萬，劃除省東賊壘百餘。

translations.literal: Yuying directed the various armies in separate suppression, recovered Xiaopianqiao and other places, and then successively defeated them at Xiaojiashan and Yingwushan, capturing and killing more than ten thousand, and clearing away more than one hundred bandit fortifications east of the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Yuying directed the various armies in separate campaigns, recovered Xiaopianqiao and other points, then successively defeated the rebels at Xiaojiashan and Yingwushan, killing or capturing more than ten thousand, and cleared away more than one hundred rebel fortifications east of the capital.

sentences.zh: 西北兩方賊仍負隅拒守，毓英令副將楊玉科、總兵李維述等規迤西，與騰越義兵約期並進。

translations.literal: Bandits in the northwest and west still held out stubbornly; Yuying ordered Vice General Yang Yuke, Military Governor Li Weishu, and others to plan the western campaign and agreed with the righteous militia of Tengyue on a date for a joint advance.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels in the northwest and west still held out stubbornly; Cen Yuying ordered Vice General Yang Yuke, Military Governor Li Weishu, and others to plan the western campaign and arranged a joint advance with the volunteer militia of Tengyue.

sentences.zh: 於是副將張保和等克富民、昆陽，總兵馬忠等克呈貢、晉寧、易門、澂江、祿豐，玉科等克武定、祿勸、元謀、羅次、定遠、大姚，維述等克廣通、楚雄、南安及黑瑯、元水諸井。

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice General Zhang Baohe and others captured Fumin and Kunyang; Military Governor Ma Zhong and others captured Chenggong, Jinning, Yimen, Chengjiang, and Lufeng; Yuke and others captured Wuding, Luquan, Yuanmou, Luoci, Dingyuan, and Dayao; Weishu and others captured Guangtong, Chuxiong, Nan'an, and the Heilang, Yuanshui, and other salt wells.
translations.idiomatic: Vice General Zhang Baohe and others took Fumin and Kunyang; Military Governor Ma Zhong and others took Chenggong, Jinning, Yimen, Chengjiang, and Lufeng; Yang Yuke and others took Wuding, Luquan, Yuanmou, Luoci, Dingyuan, and Dayao; Li Weishu and others took Guangtong, Chuxiong, Nan'an, and the Heilang, Yuanshui, and other salt wells.

sentences.zh: 凡悍酋劇匪，擒斬殆盡，省城解嚴，被詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: All fierce chieftains and major bandits were captured and executed to the last; martial law in the provincial capital was lifted, and he received an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce chieftains and major rebels were captured and executed to the last; the provincial capital stood down from martial alert, and he received an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 九年，澂江回复叛，踞府城，毓英率軍往剿，圍其郛，十年二月，克之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Hui people of Chengjiang rebelled again and held the prefectural city; Yuying led his army to suppress them, besieged the outer wall, and captured it in the second month of the tenth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Hui of Chengjiang rebelled again and held the prefectural city; Cen Yuying led his army against them, besieged the outer wall, and captured it in the second month of the tenth year.

sentences.zh: 並拔竹園、江那諸賊巢，迤西軍亦克麗江、劍川、永北、鶴慶、賓川、姚州、鎮南諸城。

translations.literal: He also captured the bandit nests at Zhuyuan, Jiangna, and other places; the western army also captured Lijiang, Jianchuan, Yongbei, Heqing, Binchuan, Yaozhou, and Zhennan and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: He also stormed the rebel nests at Zhuyuan, Jiangna, and other places; the western army also took Lijiang, Jianchuan, Yongbei, Heqing, Binchuan, Yaozhou, Zhennan, and other cities.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「滇省前事之誤，東南未定，遽議西征，屢致喪師失地。

translations.literal: He memorialized, stating: "Yunnan's earlier mistakes lay in discussing a western campaign before the southeast was settled, repeatedly causing loss of armies and territory.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "The earlier mistake in Yunnan was to push west before the southeast was secure, which repeatedly cost armies and territory.

sentences.zh: 今通籌全局，必先掃蕩東南兩迤，然後全軍西上，方無後顧之憂。」

translations.literal: Now, taking the overall situation into account, the southeast on both routes must first be swept clean, and only then may the whole army advance west, so that there will be no worries from the rear."
translations.idiomatic: We must now plan for the whole theater: secure the southeast on both routes first, then move the full army west, and only then will we be free of rearward threats."

sentences.zh: 十一年，迤東、迤西兩路悉平，西軍亦先後克復永昌、鄧川、浪穹、趙州、雲南、永平、蒙化及上下兩關，而大理賊猶堅守，恃騰越、順寧互為應援。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the eastern and western routes were both pacified; the western army also successively recovered Yongchang, Dengchuan, Langqiong, Zhaozhou, Yunnan, Yongping, Menghua, and the upper and lower passes; yet the bandits at Dali still held firm, relying on Tengyue and Shunning for mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the eastern and western routes were both pacified; the western army also recovered Yongchang, Dengchuan, Langqiong, Zhaozhou, Yunnan, Yongping, Menghua, and the upper and lower passes in turn; yet the rebels at Dali still held firm, relying on Tengyue and Shunning for mutual support.

sentences.zh: 十一月，毓英親往督戰，先斷賊援，直薄城下，掘隧道，陷城垣數十丈，奪東南兩門入。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Yuying personally went to supervise the fighting; he first cut off bandit reinforcements, pressed straight to the foot of the city wall, dug tunnels, collapsed several tens of zhang of wall, and seized the southeastern and eastern gates to enter.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Cen Yuying went in person to direct the fighting; he first severed rebel reinforcements, pressed to the foot of the walls, dug tunnels, breached several tens of zhang of wall, and stormed in through the southeastern and eastern gates.

sentences.zh: 賊守內城，晝夜環攻，守陴賊多死。

translations.literal: The bandits defended the inner city; day and night he encircled and attacked; many of the bandits defending the ramparts died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the inner city; he besieged and assaulted it day and night, and many defenders on the walls were killed.

sentences.zh: 杜文秀窮蹙服毒，其黨舁之出城詐降，斬首傳示，勒繳軍械，賊黨猶請緩期。

translations.literal: Du Wenxiu, driven to extremity, took poison; his followers carried him out of the city in a feigned surrender; his head was cut off and displayed; surrender of weapons was demanded; the bandit faction still asked for a delay.
translations.idiomatic: Du Wenxiu, driven to desperation, took poison; his followers carried him out of the city in a false surrender; his head was cut off and displayed; surrender of weapons was demanded; the rebels still asked for more time.

sentences.zh: 毓英令楊玉科率壯士二百入城受降，布重兵城外夾擊之，斬酋目三百餘名，生擒楊榮、蔡廷棟、馬仲山，磔於市。

translations.literal: Yuying ordered Yang Yuke to lead two hundred stalwart men into the city to accept the surrender; heavy troops were posted outside the city in a pincer attack; more than three hundred chieftains were beheaded; Yang Rong, Cai Tingdong, and Ma Zhongshan were captured alive and dismembered in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Yuying ordered Yang Yuke to lead two hundred picked men into the city to accept surrender; heavy forces outside the walls closed in from both sides; more than three hundred chieftains were beheaded; Yang Rong, Cai Tingdong, and Ma Zhongshan were captured alive and dismembered in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 大理肅清，賜黃馬褂，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: Dali was cleared; he was granted a yellow riding jacket and the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Dali was pacified; he was granted a yellow riding jacket and the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 十二年，順寧、雲州、騰越皆下，全滇底定，加太子少保，晉一等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Shunning, Yunzhou, and Tengyue all fell; all Yunnan was settled; he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to first-class Junior Commandant of Chariots and Cavalry with hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Shunning, Yunzhou, and Tengyue all fell; all Yunnan was settled; he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to first-class Junior Commandant of Chariots and Cavalry with hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 十三年，兼署雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he also served concurrently as Acting Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he also served concurrently as acting governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，丁繼母憂。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Guangxu reign he mourned his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Guangxu reign he went into mourning for his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 五年，服闋，授貴州巡撫，加兵部尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when mourning ended, he was appointed Governor of Guizhou and given the rank of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when his mourning ended, he was appointed governor of Guizhou and given the rank of Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 七年，調福建督辦台灣防務，開山撫番，濬大甲溪，築台北城。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Fujian to supervise Taiwan defense, open mountains and pacify the aborigines, dredge the Dajia River, and build Taipei city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to Fujian to supervise Taiwan's defenses, open the mountains and pacify the aborigines, dredge the Dajia River, and build Taipei city.

sentences.zh: 八年，署雲貴總督，九年，實授。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he served as Acting Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou; in the ninth year he received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he served as acting governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou; in the ninth year he received substantive appointment.

sentences.zh: 法越兵事起，自請出關赴前敵，屯興化。

translations.literal: When the Sino-French war broke out, he volunteered to cross the border to the front, and encamped at Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-French War began, he asked to cross the border to the front and encamped at Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 十年，命節制關外粵、楚各軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered to take overall command of the Guangdong and Huguang armies outside the pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was placed in overall command of the Cantonese and Huguang forces beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 會廣西軍潰於北寧、太原，毓英全師退屯保勝，以未奉命，降二級留任。

translations.literal: When the Guangxi army was routed at Bac Ninh and Thai Nguyen, Yuying withdrew his entire force to Baosheng; because he had not received orders, he was demoted two ranks but kept in office.
translations.idiomatic: After the Guangxi army was routed at Bac Ninh and Thai Nguyen, Cen Yuying pulled his whole force back to Baosheng. Because he had acted without orders, he was demoted two ranks but kept in his post.

sentences.zh: 七月，命進軍決戰，連复越南館司、鎮安、清波、夏和諸縣，屯館司關，規取河內諸省。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was ordered to advance for a decisive battle; he successively recovered the Vietnamese districts of Guanshi, Zhen'an, Qingbo, Xiahe, and others, encamped at Guanshi Pass, and planned to take the provinces around Hanoi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was ordered to advance for a decisive battle. He recovered Guanshi, Zhen'an, Qingbo, Xiahe, and other districts in succession, encamped at Guanshi Pass, and prepared to move on Hanoi and the surrounding provinces.

sentences.zh: 令丁槐、何秀林攻宣光，以地雷毀其城，擒斬甚眾。

translations.literal: He ordered Ding Huai and He Xiulin to attack Xuanguang; land mines destroyed the walls, and very many were captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ding Huai and He Xiulin against Xuanguang; mines brought down the walls, and a great many of the enemy were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 十一年，京察，開復降級處分，令覃修綱攻克緬旺、清水、清山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, at the capital personnel review, his demotion was restored; he ordered Tan Xiugang to capture Mianwang, Qingshui, and Qingshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, at the metropolitan review, his demotion was reversed, and he ordered Tan Xiugang to take Mianwang, Qingshui, and Qingshan.

sentences.zh: 法兵援宣光，掘地營延袤十餘裡扼之。

translations.literal: French troops reinforced Xuanguang and dug entrenchments stretching more than ten li to block the advance.
translations.idiomatic: French reinforcements reached Xuanguang and dug entrenchments more than ten li long to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 破法兵於臨洮府，奪梅枝關。

translations.literal: He defeated French troops at Linzhou Prefecture and seized Meizhi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the French at Linzhou Prefecture and seized Meizhi Pass.

sentences.zh: 連克不拔、廣威、永祥，進搗山西、河內，廣西軍亦收復諒山。

translations.literal: He successively captured Bubo, Guangwei, and Yongxiang, advanced against Son Tay and Hanoi, and the Guangxi army also recovered Lang Son.
translations.idiomatic: He took Bubo, Guangwei, and Yongxiang in succession, pressed toward Son Tay and Hanoi, and the Guangxi army recovered Lang Son as well.

sentences.zh: 越南興安、寧平、南定、興化、太原各省聞風響應。

translations.literal: The Vietnamese provinces of Xing'an, Ninh Binh, Nam Dinh, Xinghua, and Thai Nguyen all responded at the news.
translations.idiomatic: The Vietnamese provinces of Xing'an, Ninh Binh, Nam Dinh, Xinghua, and Thai Nguyen all rallied at the news.

sentences.zh: 會和議成，詔班師。

translations.literal: When peace was negotiated, an edict ordered the armies to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When a peace settlement was reached, the court ordered the armies to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 五月，回駐邊關。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he returned to garrison the border passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he returned to hold the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 十二年，會勘邊界，兼署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he joined in surveying the border and concurrently served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he took part in surveying the border and served concurrently as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 十三年，剿順寧倮黑夷匪張登發，平之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he suppressed the Luo black tribesmen under Zhang Dengfa in Shunning and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he suppressed the Black Luo tribesmen led by Zhang Dengfa in Shunning and brought the region to order.

sentences.zh: 十四年，京察，議敘。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, at the capital review, his merits were recorded for reward.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, at the metropolitan review, his service was recorded for reward.

sentences.zh: 十五年，皇太后歸政，晉太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when the Empress Dowager returned power, he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, when the Empress Dowager restored the emperor to power, he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太子太傅，入祀賢良祠，雲南、貴州建專祠，諡襄勤。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, entered the Temple of Eminent Worthies, had dedicated shrines built in Yunnan and Guizhou, and was given the posthumous name Xiangqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after. Posthumously he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, entered the Temple of Eminent Worthies, and was honored with memorial shrines in Yunnan and Guizhou under the posthumous name Xiangqin, "Assiduous and Diligent."

sentences.zh: 子春煊，官至四川總督。

translations.literal: His son Chunxuan rose to Governor-General of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chunxuan rose to become governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 弟毓寶，從毓英轉戰雲南，功最著，累擢道員，賜號額圖琿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yu Bao followed Yuying through campaigns in Yunnan with the greatest merit, was repeatedly promoted to circuit intendant, and was granted the title Etu Hui Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yu Bao followed Cen Yuying through the Yunnan campaigns with outstanding merit, rose through repeated promotions to circuit intendant, and was granted the title Etu Hui Batulu.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，出關援剿宣光、臨洮，旋克廣威府、不拔縣、梅枝關，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu he crossed the border to reinforce the campaigns at Xuanguang and Linzhou, soon captured Guangwei Prefecture, Bubo County, and Meizhi Pass, and was granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Guangxu he crossed the border to fight at Xuanguang and Linzhou, soon took Guangwei Prefecture, Bubo County, and Meizhi Pass, and was awarded the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授福建鹽法道，擢雲南按察使，權布政使，護巡撫，兼護總督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Salt and Legal Circuit Intendant of Fujian, promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Yunnan, acted as provincial treasurer, protected the governorship, and concurrently protected the governor-generalship.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed salt and legal intendant of Fujian, then promoted to surveillance commissioner of Yunnan, and served in succession as acting provincial treasurer, acting governor, and acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，調貴卅布政使，未行，復調雲南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Guizhou but did not go; he was transferred again to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was ordered to Guizhou as provincial treasurer but never went; he was reassigned to Yunnan instead.

sentences.zh: 毓寶勇於戰陣，不諳文法，御史溥松劾其護總督時，任用私人，政刑失當，坐奪職，卒於家。

translations.literal: Yu Bao was bold in battle but unversed in written law; Censor Pu Song impeached him for, while protecting the governor-generalship, employing personal favorites and mishandling government and punishment; he was stripped of office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bao was fearless in battle but ignorant of bureaucratic procedure. Censor Pu Song impeached him for favoritism and mishandling civil and criminal affairs while acting as governor-general; he was dismissed and died at home.

sentences.zh: 雲貴總督崧蕃疏陳毓寶戰功，詔復原官。

translations.literal: Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Songshen memorialized Yu Bao's battle merits, and an edict restored his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Songshen of Yunnan-Guizhou memorialized Yu Bao's military service, and the throne restored his former rank.

sentences.zh: 論曰：劉長佑樸誠廉毅，老於軍事，時病其失之慈柔。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Liu Zhangyou was plain, sincere, incorruptible, and resolute, experienced in military affairs, though at the time people criticized him for excessive leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Liu Zhangyou was plainspoken, sincere, incorruptible, and firm, seasoned in military affairs—though contemporaries faulted him for excessive leniency.

sentences.zh: 自言：「於是非邪正，不自欺以欺人。」

translations.literal: He himself said: "In matters of right and wrong, good and evil, I do not deceive myself in order to deceive others."
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "On questions of right and wrong, I do not deceive myself in order to deceive others."

sentences.zh: 非飾辭也。

translations.literal: This was no mere ornament of speech.
translations.idiomatic: That was no mere figure of speech.

sentences.zh: 滇、粵籌邊，尤有遠見。

translations.literal: In planning the defenses of Yunnan and Guangdong he showed especially far-sighted judgment.
translations.idiomatic: In securing the Yunnan and Guangdong frontiers he showed exceptional foresight.

sentences.zh: 劉岳昭治滇，能屈己以聽岑毓英。

translations.literal: Liu Yuezhao, in governing Yunnan, was able to humble himself and heed Cen Yuying.
translations.idiomatic: In governing Yunnan, Liu Yuezhao was willing to set pride aside and follow Cen Yuying's lead.

sentences.zh: 毓英與滇事相終始，跋扈霸才，竟成戡定偉績，信乎識時之傑，能自樹立者已。

translations.literal: Yuying was involved in Yunnan affairs from beginning to end; overbearing yet gifted, he nevertheless achieved the great feat of pacification—truly a hero who knew the times and could stand on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Yuying shaped Yunnan's fate from first to last: domineering yet gifted, he nonetheless brought the province to lasting peace—a man who read the times aright and made his own place in history.
